ASAD-NOTES:15:intro/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:intro/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:intro/r4.claim: The surah's main theme is God's creative activity and guidance through revelation, especially the Qur'an, which verse 9 predicts will remain incorruptible.
ASAD-NOTES:15:intro/r4.anchor: the Qur'an, which, as verse 9 pred icts, will for all times remain impervious to corruption

SAMIN-DURR:15:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:15:9/r1.claim: نحن may be the subject or an emphatic pronoun; it cannot be a separator because it does not occur between two nouns.
SAMIN-DURR:15:9/r1.anchor: إما مبتدأ، وإما تأكيد، ولا يكون فصلا لأنه لم يقع بين اسمين

SAMIN-DURR:15:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:15:9/r2.claim: The pronoun in له most naturally refers to the Reminder; an alternative takes it to refer to the Messenger.
SAMIN-DURR:15:9/r2.anchor: والضمير في " له " للذكر، وهو الظاهر. وقيل: للرسول عليه السلام

ZAJJAJ:v3p174/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p174/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p174/r1.claim: God preserves the Reminder from any addition or subtraction, as 41:42 also says.
ZAJJAJ:v3p174/r1.anchor: أي نحفظه من أن يقع فيه زيادة أو نقصان، كما قال: (لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه

ASAD-NOTES:15:8/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:8/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:8/r2.claim: God says that He revealed the reminder in stages and will preserve it from corruption.
ASAD-NOTES:15:8/r2.anchor: this reminder? and, behold, it is We who shall truly guard it [from all corruption]

ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n9/r1.claim: The reminder is the Qur'an; the form nazzalna indicates gradual revelation, as Zamakhshari notes on 2:23 and Asad's note 14 there explains.
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n9/r1.anchor: I.e., the Qur'an. The grammatical form nazzalnd implies a gradual revelation ("step by step") over a period of time

ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n10/r1.claim: Asad says the prophecy is confirmed by the Qur'an's unchanged text since the seventh century, and claims no other book has been preserved similarly for so long.
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n10/r1.anchor: the text of the Qur'an has remained free from all alterations, additions or deletions ever since it was enunciated by the Prophet in the seventh century

ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n10/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n10/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n10/r2.claim: Early variants reported by classical commentators concern diacritical marks or vocalization and generally do not change meaning; Asad also refers to lawh mahfuz in 85:22.
ASAD-NOTES:15:8#n10/r2.anchor: differences in respect of diacritical marks or of vocalisation, and, as a rule, do not affect the meaning of the passage in question

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: This promise reassures the Prophet: the Book came from God rather than the Prophet’s desire, and God himself will preserve it, so rejection by Quraysh should not distress him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this Book has been revealed by God not as a result of his desire and He Himself will protect it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: If Quraysh reject the Qur’an, God will raise other recipients who accept it and sacrifice to call people to it and protect it; Islahi cites al-An‘ām 6:89 and says acceptance benefits them while rejection brings their doom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: if these people deny, do not be aggrieved; We will consign it to some others who will not deny

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God inclined the Anṣār to accept the Qur’an wholeheartedly and sacrifice everything to protect it, one historical means by which His preservation promise was fulfilled.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: inclined the hearts of the Anṣā r towards it; they whole-heartedly accepted it and sacrificed everything to protect it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The wording that God Himself sent the Book down carries double emphasis.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: has a double emphasis in it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet’s duty is to convey the Book, not to make people accept it; it was not sent at his request.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he does not have the responsibility to make people accept it. His responsibility is to only convey it to others.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Preserving the Book intact is God’s responsibility, and history shows the many ways He fulfilled this promise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: As far as keeping it intact and its protection is concerned, God will take care of it.

NASHR:v1p4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p4/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p4/r1.claim: God uniquely undertook to preserve the Qurʾan without entrusting it to the community, unlike earlier scriptures; the author cites the Torah’s being entrusted to its custodians as the contrast.
NASHR:v1p4/r1.anchor: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

NASHR:v1p4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p4/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p4/r2.claim: The preservation and inimitability of the Qurʾan attest to Muḥammad’s prophethood: eloquent, hostile Arabs could not produce even a verse to match it, and it endured recitation for over eight centuries despite opponents.
NASHR:v1p4/r2.anchor: تحدى بسورة منه أفصح العرب لسانا وأعظمهم عنادا وعتوا وإنكارا فلم يقدروا على أن يأتوا بآية مثله

NASHR:v1p4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p4/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p4/r3.claim: The Qurʾan is an inexhaustible source of proofs, arguments, and wisdoms, so this community did not need a succession of prophets as earlier communities did; their prophets governed by scripture and guided them.
NASHR:v1p4/r3.anchor: ومن ثم لم تحتج هذه الأمة إلى نبي بعد نبيها - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كما كانت الأمم قبل ذلك

NASHR:v1p4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p4/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p4/r4.claim: God says He caused those He chose among His servants to inherit the Book, and the author links this chosen group with those granted preservation.
NASHR:v1p4/r4.anchor: ولما تكفل تعالى بحفظه خص به من شاء من بريته، وأورثه

NASHR:v1p4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p4/r5.speaker: النبي
NASHR:v1p4/r5.claim: A report from Anas states that God has chosen people who are His own and special; Ibn Mājah, Aḥmad, al-Dārimī and others transmit it with narrators the author grades trustworthy.
NASHR:v1p4/r5.anchor: إن لله أهلين من الناس، قيل: من هم يا رسول الله؟ قال: أهل القرآن هم أهل الله وخاصته

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p345#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p345#2/r1.speaker: قتادة وثابت
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p345#2/r1.claim: Qatada and Thabit say God preserves the Reminder from Satan adding falsehood to it or removing truth from it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p345#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة وثابت في قوله تعالى ﴿ إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون ﴾ قال حفظه الله من أن يزيد فيه الشيطان باطلا أو يبطل منه حقا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r1.claim: God answers their denial of revelation and mockery of His Messenger, while consoling the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r1.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى رد إنكارهم التنزيل واستهزاءهم برسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r2.claim: ‘We’ and ‘indeed We’ express God’s majesty; the emphatic wording affirms that He Himself sent down the Qurʾān.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r2.anchor: أي نحن بعظم شأننا وعلو جانبنا نزلنا الذكر أنكروه وأنكروا نزوله عليك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r3.claim: Al-dhikr is the Qurʾān; the disbelievers deny its descent and ridicule the Prophet for claiming it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r3.anchor: نزلنا الذكر أنكروه وأنكروا نزوله عليك وقالوا فيك لادعائه ما قالوا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r4.claim: God protects the Qurʾān from anything that would impair it, including distortion, additions, omissions, mockery, and denial; preservation means such attacks have no effect and are repelled.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r4.anchor: أي من أكل ما يقدح فيه كالتحريف والزيادة والنقصان وغير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets preservation as keeping the revealed law in force until the Day of Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن : حفظه بابقاء شريعته إلى يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r6.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r6.claim: Other commentators understand the nominal sentence as continuous miraculous protection from additions, omissions, distortion, and alteration; earlier scriptures were entrusted to religious scholars and suffered corruption, whereas God Himself preserves the Qurʾān.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r6.anchor: وجوز غير واحد أن يراد حفظه بالإعجاز في كل وقت كما يدل عليه الجملة الأسمية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r7.speaker: الكشاف والكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r7.claim: Al-Kashshāf asks why append preservation after the assertion of sending; al-Kashf answers that it adds enduring preservation and makes the Qurʾān’s miraculous inimitability evidence of divine origin, since additions or omissions would break its form.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p15#2/r7.anchor: سأل بما حاصله أن الكلام لما كان مسوقا لردهم وقد تم الجواب بالأول فما فائدة التذييل بالثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r1.claim: Inimitability alone cannot prevent omission of whole sūras without harming the Qurʾān’s miraculousness. The preferred account is that God preserves it as revealed by miraculousness and other means, including enabling the Companions to collect it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r1.anchor: أن الإعجاز لا يكون سببا لحفظه عن إسقاط بعض السور لأن ذلك لا يخل بالإعجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r2.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r2.claim: Al-Qāḍī cites the verse against an Imāmī claim that additions or omissions entered the Qurʾān; al-Rāzī calls the argument circular because those claimants could say this verse itself was added, and the asserted inimitability of this amount needs proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r2.anchor: واحتج القاضي بالآية على فساد قول بعض من الإمامية لا يعبأ بهم إن القرآن قد دخله الزيادة والنقصان

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r3.speaker: القائلون بحدوث الكلام اللفظي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r3.claim: Those who hold that verbal Qurʾānic speech is originated also cite this verse as evidence, which al-Ālūsī says appears to support their view.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r3.anchor: واحتج بها القائلون بحدوث الكلام اللفظي وهي ظاهرة فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r4.speaker: أصحاب القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī’s associates infer that the basmala is a verse of every sūra: otherwise the promised preservation would allow an addition, and suspecting the Companions of adding it would also invite suspicion of omission and undermine the Qurʾān as proof; al-Ālūsī derides this as a nonsensical argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r4.anchor: قال أصحابنا في هذه الآية دلالة على كون البسملة آية من كل سورة لأن الله تعالى قد وعد حفظ القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r5.claim: Wa-naḥnu is not a pronoun of separation because it does not fall between two nouns; it is either a new subject or an emphatic pronoun for the name in inna.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r5.anchor: ( ونحن ) ليس فصلا لأنه لم يقع بين اسمين وإنما هو إما مبتدأ أو توكيد لاسم إن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r6.claim: The paired clauses and their emphases display divine majesty and the grandeur of the revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في سبك الجملتين من الدلالة على كمال الكبرياء والجلالة وعلى فخامة شأن التنزيل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والأكثرون
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r7.claim: Mujāhid, Qatāda, and most authorities take ‘it’ to refer to the Qurʾān, the apparent reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r7.anchor: وإليه ذهب مجاهد وقتادة والأكثرون وهو الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r8.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and a small minority take the pronoun to refer to the Prophet, meaning God protects him from the plot of the mockers, as in 5:67; al-Ālūsī prefers the Qurʾān as antecedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r8.anchor: وجوز الفراء وذهب إليه النزر أن يكون راجعا إلى النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r9.claim: The preservation answer comes after the direct answer about revelation because of the previously noted rhetorical reason and its connection to the following passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p16/r9.anchor: وأخر هذا الجواب مع أنه رد لأول كلامهم الباطل لما أشرنا إليه فيما مر ولارتباطه بما يعقبه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r4.claim: God protects the Qur'an from devils adding, subtracting, or changing it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r4.anchor: {إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر} يعني القرآن {وإنا له لحافظون} أي: نحفظ القرآن من الشياطين أن يزيدوا فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r5.claim: Baghawī cites that falsehood cannot approach the Qur'an and identifies falsehood as Iblīs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r5.anchor: والباطل: هو إبليس، لا يقدر أن يزيد فيه ما ليس منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r6.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun to refer to Muḥammad, whom God protects from harm.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r6.anchor: وقيل الهاء في "له" راجعة إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أي: إنا لمحمد لحافظون ممن أراده بسوء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r7.claim: The alternative is supported by the statement that God protects the Messenger from people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p369#2/r7.anchor: كما قال جل ذكره: {والله يعصمك من الناس}

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r6.claim: The emphatic declaration rebuts their denial and mockery, affirming that God sent down the Reminder.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r6.anchor: رد لإنكارهم واستهزائهم ولذلك أكده من وجوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r7.claim: God protects the Qur’an from alteration, additions, and omissions by making its inimitable wording distinguishable from human speech to Arabic speakers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r7.anchor: أي من التحريف والزيادة والنقص بأن جعلناه معجزا مباينا لكلام البشر، بحيث لا يخفى تغيير نظمه على أهل اللسان

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r8.claim: Alternatively, the verse guarantees that the Qur’an will remain free of error over time.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r8.anchor: أو نفي تطرق الخلل إليه في الدوام بضمان الحفظ له

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r9.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r9.claim: A reported alternative takes the pronoun to refer to the Prophet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:7-9/r9.anchor: وقيل الضمير في { له } للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r5.claim: The emphatic We declares that God alone, not jinn or humans, sent down the Reminder gradually through Gabriel, answering the claim that a jinn confuses Muhammad.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r5.anchor: أي على ما لنا من العظمة لا غيرنا من جن ولا إنس

BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r6.claim: Here the Reminder denotes both admonition and honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r6.anchor: أي الموعظة والشرف { وإنا له } أي بعظمتنا وإن رغمت

BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r7.claim: God preserves the Reminder perpetually through His power and knowledge; its divine preservation rules out its being the confused speech of a madman.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r8.claim: The Prophet's sound reason, high resolve, certainty, precision, trustworthy judgment and firmness likewise contradict the charge of madness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r8.anchor: يعلمون أنك أكملهم عقلا , وأعلاهم همة , وأيقنهم فكرا , وأتقنهم أمرا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r9.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r9.claim: Al-Bukhari reports Zayd's account that after Yamama's heavy losses among Qur'an reciters, Umar persuaded Abu Bakr to commission Zayd to gather the Qur'an from written materials and people's memories; Zayd found al-Tawba's closing verses only with Khuzaima, or Abu Khuzaima, al-Ansari.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r9.anchor: روى البخاري في التفسير والفتن عن زيد بين ثابت رضي الله عنه قال : أرسل إلي أبو بكر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r10.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r10.claim: Zayd's report says the compiled sheets remained with Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Hafsa, showing their custody after the first collection.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r10.anchor: وكانت الصحف التي جمع فيها القرآن عند أبي بكر حتى توفاه الله تعالى ثم عند عمر حتى توفاه الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r11.speaker: أنس
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r11.claim: Anas reports that Hudhayfa feared divergent recitations among Syrian and Iraqi forces; Uthman borrowed Hafsa's sheets and tasked Zayd, Ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id b. al-As, and Abd al-Rahman b. al-Harith to copy, use Quraysh dialect for disputes and burn other copies.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r11.anchor: وروي بعده عن أنس رضي الله عنه أن حذيفة بن اليمان رضي الله عنه قدم على عثمان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r12.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r12.claim: Zayd reports that a verse of al-Ahzab he often heard the Prophet recite was missing from the collected codices and found only with Khuzaima, whose testimony counted as that of two men.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p206/r12.anchor: وله عن خارجة بن زيد بن ثابت أنه سمع زيد بن ثابت رضي الله عنه قال : لما نسخنا الصحف

DURR-FULL:v5p66/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses God’s preservation of the Reminder as its being with Him.
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {وإنا له لحافظون} قال: عندنا

DURR-FULL:v5p66/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r7.claim: Qatada says God sent down and preserved the Qur’an; Iblis can neither insert falsehood nor remove truth, as also stated in 41:42.
DURR-FULL:v5p66/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون} وقال

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r2.claim: The emphatic نحن magnifies God’s majesty and exalted rank.

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r3.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r3.claim: Al-Kawāshī says نحن is not a separator because it stands between two nouns; it is instead a subject.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r3.anchor: ونحن ليست بفصل لأنها بين اسمين وإنما هي مبتدأ كما في الكواشي

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r4.claim: The Reminder is the Book deniers rejected and whose revelation to Muhammad they denied; they accused him of madness and obscured its Revealer by using the passive form.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r4.anchor: ذلك الذكر الذي أنكروه وأنكروا نزوله عليك ونسبوك بذلك إلى الجنون

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r5.claim: Al-Kāshifī says dhikr can mean honor: the Book brings honor and glory in this world and the next, as in 23:71.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وذكر بمعنى شرف نيز مى آيد

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r6.claim: God preserves the Quran from attacks, denial, mockery, distortion, alteration, addition, and deletion.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r6.anchor: كالطعن فيه والمجادلة في حقيته والتكذيب له والاستهزاء به

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r7.claim: Earlier scriptures developed errors because God did not undertake to preserve them and entrusted their keeping to people.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r7.anchor: وأما الكتب المتقدمة فلما لم يتول حفظها واستحفظها الناس تطرق إليها الخلل

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r8.speaker: التبيان
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r8.claim: Al-Tibyān says God guards the Quran against devils’ whispers and mixtures, preventing false additions and deletion of truth.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r8.anchor: وفي التبيان أو حافظون له من الشياطين من وساوسهم

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r9.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r9.claim: Baḥr al-ʿUlūm explains preservation as ṣarfah: people could alter or diminish the Quran as earlier scriptures, but God turned them away from it.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r9.anchor: في بحر العلوم : حفظه إياه بالصرفة على معنى أن الناس كانوا قادرين

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r10.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r10.claim: He also explains preservation through scholars and their works on the Quran’s wording and meanings, including tafsir and readings.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r10.anchor: أو بحفظ العلماء وتصنيفهم الكتب التي صنفوها في شرح الفاظه ومعانيه

BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r11.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r11.claim: The Mathnawī says God promised the Quranic lesson would not die with Muhammad and guards the miraculous Book from increase and decrease.
BURSEVI:v4p293#3/r11.anchor:
في المثنوى :
مصطفى را وعده كرد الطاف حق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r1.claim: The verse begins by refuting their mockery in 15:6, after the answer to their challenge to produce angels in 15:7; the two replies are unfolded in reverse order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r1.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي لإبطال جزء من كلامهم المستهزئين به ، إذ قالوا : { يأيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r2.claim: The reply uses their own premise—affirming that the Reminder was sent to the Messenger—to silence their ridicule, and stresses the true statement with inna and the separating pronoun, as in 63:1.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r2.anchor: وكان هذا الجواب من نوع القول بالموجب بتقرير إنزال الذكر على الرسول مجاراة لظاهر كلامهم . والمقصود الرد عليهم في استهزائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r3.claim: The parenthetical second clause escalates the rebuke: the sender of the Reminder himself preserves it; the wāw is parenthetic and the pronoun refers to the Reminder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r3.anchor: بأن منزل الذكر هو حافظه من كيد الأعداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r4.claim: The lām strengthens the verb's effect because the verb comes after its object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r4.anchor: واللام لتقوية عمل العامل لضعفه بالتأخير عن معموله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r5.claim: Preservation includes preventing the Reminder from vanishing, being added to or diminished, or being altered; God facilitated mass transmission and memorization from the Prophet's lifetime.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r5.anchor: وشمل حفظه الحفظ من التلاشي ، والحفظ من الزيادة والنقصان فيه ، بأن يسر تواتره وأسباب ذلك ، وسلمه من التبديل والتغيير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r6.speaker: القاضي إسماعيل بن إسحاق بن حماد المالكي البصري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r6.claim: As related by Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq explained that earlier books changed because God entrusted their scholars with preservation, whereas God preserves the Qur'an himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p20/r6.anchor: أن القاضي إسماعيل بن إسحاق بن حماد المالكي البصري سئل عن السر في تطرق التغيير للكتب السالفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن بن المنتاب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r1.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan ibn al-Muntāb repeated Ismāʿīl's explanation to al-Muḥāmilī, who replied that no statement could be better.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r1.anchor: قال أبو الحسن بن المنتاب ذكرت هذا الكلام للمحاملي فقال لي : لا أحسن من هذا الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r2.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r2.claim: A report in al-Qurṭubī, attributed there to Yaḥyā ibn Aktham, recounts Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna saying prior scripture was entrusted to its people and lost, while God guards the Qur'an so it is not lost.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير ( القرطبي ) في خبر رواه عن يحيى بن أكثم : أنه ذكر قصة إسلام رجل يهودي في زمن المأمون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr suggests the parallel explanations may be a coincidence of independent thoughts.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r4.claim: The promise honors the Qur'an and angers the polytheists by announcing that the religion will prevail and the Qur'an endure through the ages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r4.anchor: وفي هذا مع التنويه بشأن القرآن إغاظة للمشركين بأن أمر هذا الدين سيتم وينتشر القرآن ويبقى على ممر الأزمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r5.claim: Its endurance is a challenge and sign of the Messenger's truth: a human composition or non-miracle would admit corruption and contradiction, unlike the Qur'an (4:82).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p21/r5.anchor: وهذا من التحدي ليكون هذا الكلام كالدليل على أن القرآن منزل من عند الله آية على صدق الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r1.claim: The emphatic reply answers their mockery, like answering a sarcastic ‘great one’ with ‘yes, I am great.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر رد على المستخفين في قولهم: يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r2.claim: One group takes ‘it’ to refer to Muhammad: God protects him from their harm and plots; al-Ṭabarī reports this view without attribution.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r2.anchor: قالت فرقة: الضمير في له عائد على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، أي يحفظه من أذاكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r3.claim: The majority, including Mujāhid and Qatāda, take ‘it’ to refer to the Qurʾān, which God preserves from alteration and change.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة- وهي الأكثر- الضمير في له عائد على القرآن وقاله مجاهد وقتادة، والمعنى: لحافظون من أن يبدل أو يغير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r4.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says earlier books were altered in interpretation, not wording; the author says Qurʾānic verses show that wording was changed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r4.anchor: وفي آخر ورقة من البخاري عن ابن عباس: أن التبديل فيها إنما كان في التأويل وأما في اللفظ فلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r5.claim: The apparent evidence shows verbal alteration; placing a hand over the stoning verse is itself a kind of alteration of wording, and the preservation explanations are close in meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r5.anchor: وظاهر آيات القرآن أنهم بدلوا اللفظ، ووضع اليد في آية الرجم هو في معنى تبديل الألفاظ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r6.claim: Another reported explanation is that God preserves the Qurʾān by storing it in people’s breasts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: لحافظون باختزانه في صدور الرجال.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r7.claim: Qatāda connects this promise to the declaration that falsehood cannot approach the Qurʾān from before or behind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p351#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: هذه الآية نحو قوله تعالى: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r4.claim: God Himself revealed the Qurʾan, the Remembrance, and protects it from alteration or replacement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r4.anchor: أنه هو الذي أنزل الذكر، وهو القرآن، وهو الحافظ له من التغيير والتبديل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r5.claim: Some take the pronoun in “its guardian” to refer to the Prophet, supported by 5:67, where God promises to protect him from people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r5.anchor: ومنهم من أعاد الضمير في قوله تعالى: {له لحافظون} على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، كقوله: {والله يعصمك من الناس}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr prefers the pronoun's reference to the Qurʾan because that is the apparent sense of the surrounding passage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p527/r6.anchor: والمعنى الأول أولى، وهو ظاهر السياق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r1.claim: The emphatic opening answers the mockery of 15:6 by asserting decisively that God Himself sent the Reminder through Gabriel to Muḥammad.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r1.anchor: رد لإنكارهم واستهزائهم في قولهم : { وقالوا يأيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r2.claim: God guards the Quran from devils and from addition, omission, distortion, and alteration at every time; earlier scriptures were entrusted to rabbis and scholars, who altered them through envy and disagreement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r2.anchor: محفوظا من الشياطين وهو حافظه في كل وقت من كل زيادة ونقصان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r3.claim: Divine preservation also demonstrates that the Quran is revealed: human speech would be exposed to additions and omissions like other speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r3.anchor: قد جعل ذلك دليلا على أنه منزل من عنده آية ؛ لأنه لو كان من قول البشر أو غير آية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r4.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun له to refer to the Messenger, as in God's promise to protect him in 5:67.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p535#4/r4.anchor: وقيل : الضمير في { له } لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كقوله تعالى { والله يعصمك }

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r7.claim: One interpretation takes “We will preserve it” to mean that God protects Muhammad from enemies who seek to harm him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r7.anchor: وإنا لمحمد حافظون ممن أراده بسوء من أعدائه , حكاه ابن جرير

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, “it” is the Quran, which God preserves.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r9.claim: Preserving the Quran means keeping it until it is requited for on Judgment Day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r9.anchor: حفظه حتى يجزى به يوم القيامة , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r10.claim: God protects the Quran from Satan adding falsehood to it or removing truth from it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r10.anchor: حفظه من أن يزيد فيه الشيطان باطلا , أو يزيل منه حقا , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r11.claim: God preserves the Quran in those He wills good for and removes it from the hearts of those He wills evil for.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p148#2/r11.anchor: إنا له لحافظون في قلوب من أردنا به خيرا , وذاهبوان به من قلوب من أردنا به شرا

MUJAHID:v1p339#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p339#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p339#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses God's keeping of the Reminder as keeping it with Him.
MUJAHID:v1p339#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وإنا له لحافظون ﴾ أي عندنا

MUQATIL:15:8-9/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:15:8-9/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:15:8-9/r2.claim: The reminder is the Quran revealed to Muhammad; God protects it because satans cannot reach it, rebutting the claim that a satan teaches the Prophet.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r1.claim: Al-dhikr is the Qurʾān; the preservation promise answers the unbelievers' denial and mockery in 15:6.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r1.anchor: وهو رد لانكارهم واستهزائهم في قولهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r2.claim: God preserves the Qurʾān from satans and at all times from addition, subtraction, distortion, and alteration.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r2.anchor: محفوظا من الشياطين وهو حافظه في كل وقت من الزيادة والنقصان والتحريف والتبديل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r3.claim: Earlier scriptures were entrusted to rabbis and scholars rather than divinely preserved; their envy-driven disputes led to distortion, whereas the Qurʾān was not left in others' care.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r3.anchor: فإنه لم يتول حفظها وإنما استحفظها الربانيين والاحبار فاختلفوا فيما بينهم بغيا فوقع التحريف

NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r4.claim: God's preservation is evidence that the Qurʾān was revealed by Him: human speech would be vulnerable to additions and omissions.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r4.anchor: دليلا على أنه منزل من عنده آية اذ لو كان من قول البشر أو غير آية لتطرق عليه الزيادة والنقصان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the Messenger, as in God's promise to protect him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p238#3/r5.anchor: أو الضمير في له لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كقوله والله يعصمك

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r1.claim: The الذكر sent down here is the Qurʾān.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر } يعني القرآن.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r2.claim: God preserves the Qurʾān from additions and omissions.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r2.anchor: { وإنا له لحافظون } من أن يزاد فيه أو ينقص منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r3.speaker: قتادة وثابت البناني
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r3.claim: Qatāda and Thābit al-Bunānī say God protects it from Satanic additions of falsehood or removal of truth, and has kept it preserved ever since.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r3.anchor: قال قتادة وثابت البناني: حفظه الله من أن تزيد فيه الشياطين باطلا أو تنقص منه حقا فتولى سبحانه حفظه فلم يزل محفوظا،

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r4.claim: The author contrasts the Qurʾān, which God preserves, with earlier scripture whose custodians were entrusted with its preservation and altered it.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r4.anchor: وقال في غيره: بما استحفظوا [المائدة: 44]، فوكل حفظه إليهم فبدلوا وغيروا.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r5.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r5.claim: Yahyā ibn Aktham recounts that a Jewish scholar tested scriptures by altering copies: Torah and Gospel buyers accepted them, but Qurʾān copyists detected changes and rejected them, prompting his conversion.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r5.anchor: يحيى بن أكثم يقول: كان للمأمون وهو أمير إذ ذاك مجلس نظر، فدخل في جملة الناس رجل يهودي حسن الثوب

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r6.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r6.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna validates the preservation contrast through 5:44: custodians lost the scripture entrusted to them, whereas God preserved the Qurʾān for the community.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9/r6.anchor: فلقيت سفيان بن عيينة فذكرت له الخبر فقال لي: مصداق هذا في كتاب الله عز وجل. قال قلت: في أي موضع؟

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r1.claim: The author explains the cited 5:44 contrast: preservation was entrusted to earlier custodians and lost, while God preserved the Qurʾān for the community.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r1.anchor: بما استحفظوا من كتاب الله [المائدة: 44]، فجعل حفظه إليهم فضاع

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r2.claim: One interpretation takes the pronoun as Muhammad: God protects him from falsely claiming something about God or having a false claim made against him.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: «وإنا له لحافظون» أي لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من أن يتقول علينا أو نتقول عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation says God protects Muhammad from being plotted against or killed, paralleling 5:67.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r3.anchor: أو «وإنا له لحافظون» من أن يكاد أو يقتل. نظيره والله يعصمك من الناس [المائدة: 67].

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r4.claim: نحن can be a nominative subject whose predicate is نزلنا, with the whole clause serving as the predicate of إن.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r4.anchor: و«نحن» يجوز أن يكون موضعه رفعا بالابتداء و«نزلنا» الخبر. والجملة خبر «إن».

QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, نحن is emphatic in the accusative referring to إن’s noun; it is not a separator because the following clause is indefinite and clauses can modify indefinite nouns.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:9#2/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «نحن» تأكيدا لاسم «إن» في موضع نصب، ولا تكون فاصلة لأن الذي بعدها ليس بمعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v19p126#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p126#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p126#2/r9.claim: The preservation declaration confirms the Prophet's earlier statement that God sent down the Reminder to him, which prompted their mocking address.
RAZI-FULL:v19p126#2/r9.anchor: أن القوم إنما قالوا : { وقالوا يأيها الذى نزل عليه الذكر } ( الحجر : 6 ) لأجل أنهم سمعوا النبي

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r1.claim: The first-person plural is a royal form of majesty; a single monarch says we did or said something to magnify the act.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r1.anchor: فهذه الصيغة وإن كانت للجمع إلا أن هذا من كلام الملوك عند إظهار التعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers the pronoun's return to the Reminder: God protects it from distortion, additions, and omissions, as other verses affirm its integrity.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r2.anchor: القول الأول : أنه عائد إلى الذكر يعني : وإنا نحفظ ذلك الذكر من التحريف والزيادة والنقصان

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r3.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r3.claim: An objection asks why the Companions compiled the Qur'an into a codex if God's promise already guaranteed its preservation.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r3.anchor: فإن قيل : فلم اشتغلت الصحابة بجمع القرآن في المصحف وقد وعد الله تعالى بحفظه

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r4.claim: The Companions' compilation was itself one of the means by which God preserved the Qur'an, appointing them to that task.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r4.anchor: والجواب : أن جمعهم للقرآن كان من أسباب حفظ الله تعالى إياه فإنه تعالى لما أن حفظه قيضهم لذلك

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī's associates argue that preservation proves the basmala belongs to the Qur'an at the start of every sūra; otherwise the text would be exposed to addition or alteration.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r5.anchor: قال أصحابنا : وفي هذه الآية دلالة قوية على كون التسمية آية من أول كل سورة

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r6.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r6.claim: They add that if the Companions could be suspected of inserting text, they could also be suspected of omitting it, undermining the Qur'an's status as proof.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r6.anchor: وذلك يوجب خروج القرآن عن كونه حجة

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r7.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ offers the alternative that the pronoun refers to Muhammad: God is his protector.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r7.anchor: أن الكناية في قوله : { له } راجعة إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والمعنى وإنا لمحمد لحافظون وهو قول الفراء

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī supports the Muhammad referent: mentioning the revelation and what was revealed makes its recipient an understood referent, as in the pronoun for Qur'an in 97:1.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r8.anchor: وقوى ابن الأنباري هذا القول فقال : لما ذكر الله الإنزال والمنزل دل ذلك على المنزل عليه

RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r9.claim: Despite the alternative, Al-Rāzī judges the Qur'an referent stronger and more faithful to the verse's apparent wording.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127/r9.anchor: إلا أن القول الأول أرجح القولين وأحسنهما مشابهة لظاهر التنزيل

RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r1.claim: One account says God preserves the Qur'an by making it miraculous and unlike human speech, so additions or deletions disrupt its order and are recognized as alien.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : حفظه بأن جعله معجزا مباينا لكلام البشر فعجز الخلق عن الزيادة فيه والنقصان عنه

RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r2.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r2.claim: Another account says God protected the Qur'an by making creatures incapable of producing a rival to it.

RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r3.claim: Another account says God prevented corruption by appointing a community to memorize, study, and publicize the Qur'an for as long as religious obligation remains.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : أعجز الخلق عن إبطاله وإفساده بأن قيض جماعة يحفظونه ويدرسونه ويشهرونه فيما بين الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r4.claim: Another account says any attempt to change a letter or dot would be exposed by the community, even children correcting an eminent elder's slip.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون : المراد بالحفظ هو أن أحدا لو حاول تغييره بحرف أو نقطة لقال له أهل الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r5.claim: No other scripture has remained free of copying errors and alteration, while the Qur'an remains protected despite the strong motives of heretics, Jews, and Christians to corrupt it; this is a great miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r5.anchor: واعلم أنه لم يتفق لشيء من الكتب مثل هذا الحفظ ، فإنه لا كتاب إلا وقد دخله التصحيف والتحريف والتغيير

RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r6.claim: The Qur'an's continued preservation for nearly six centuries after God's prediction is knowledge of the unseen and another decisive miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r6.anchor: وأيضا أخبر الله تعالى عن بقائه محفوظا عن التغيير والتحريف ، وانقضى الآن قريبا من ستمائة سنة

RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī uses the preservation promise to refute some Imāmīs who claim the Qur'an acquired additions, omissions, or alterations.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r7.anchor: احتج القاضي بقوله : { إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون } على فساد قول بعض الإمامية

RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī calls that proof weak and circular: Imāmīs could say this very preservation verse is one of the additions they allege.
RAZI-FULL:v19p127#2/r8.anchor: فثبت أن إثبات هذا المطلوب بهذه الآية يجري مجرى إثبات الشيء نفسه

STUDYQURAN:15:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r1.claim: As in 15:6, the Reminder here refers to the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r1.anchor: For the Reminder as a reference to the Quran, see v. 6

STUDYQURAN:15:9/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r2.claim: The promise to preserve the Quran means God protects its text from alteration or additions; 41:42 and 4:82 support this reading.
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r2.anchor: God will protect the Quran from any alterations or additions to its words

STUDYQURAN:15:9/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r3.speaker: Muslims
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r3.claim: Muslims hold that the Quran cannot be falsified because believers widely memorize, study, and transmit it.
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r3.anchor: Muslims maintain that the Quran is not susceptible to being falsified, owing to the widespread manner in which it has been memorized, studied, and proliferated among believers

STUDYQURAN:15:9/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r4.speaker: another interpretation
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r4.claim: Another interpretation says divine protection includes the Quran's miraculous arrangement, like walls fortifying and protecting a city.
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r4.anchor: It is also said that God’s Protection of the Quran extends to the miraculous nature of its order

STUDYQURAN:15:9/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r5.speaker: another interpretation
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r5.claim: Another interpretation says God preserves the Quran through its traditional reciters, whose hearts are treasuries of His Book.
STUDYQURAN:15:9/r5.anchor: According to another interpretation, God preserves the Quran through the Quran reciters

TAB-FULL:v14p18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says that the pronoun in “for it” refers to the Reminder, the Quran.
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r1.anchor: «له» من ذكر الذكر. وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v14p18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the promise of preservation as “with Us.”
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وإنا له لحافظون} [الحجر: 9] قال: «عندنا»

TAB-FULL:v14p18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r3.claim: Qatadah connects this promise to 41:42: falsehood is Iblis, and God preserved the Quran so Satan cannot add falsehood or remove truth.
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: {وإنا له لحافظون} [الحجر: 9] قال: «حفظه الله من أن يزيد فيه الشيطان باطلا، أو ينقص منه حقا»

TAB-FULL:v14p18/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r4.speaker: قيل
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r4.claim: An alternative view takes the pronoun to refer to Muhammad, meaning God protects him from enemies who wish him harm.
TAB-FULL:v14p18/r4.anchor: وقيل: الهاء في قوله: {وإنا له لحافظون} [الحجر: 9] من ذكر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

SULAMI:v1p350#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r1.claim: Ibn Ata reads the revealed Reminder as healing, mercy, clarification, and criterion that guides those destined for felicity and protects them from disobedience.
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : نحن نزلنا الذكر شفاء

SULAMI:v1p350#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r2.claim: God preserves the Reminder in the hearts of His friends and employs the limbs of His elect servants in its service.
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أي حفظه في قلوب أوليائه ويستعمل

SULAMI:v1p350#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r3.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r3.claim: Ja'far says God's preservation accompanies those for whom He wills good through the span of life.
SULAMI:v1p350#3/r3.anchor: وقال جعفر : ﴿ وإنا له لحافظون ﴾ على من أردنا به خيرا

TABATABAI:15:9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9/r1.claim: The sūra addresses unbelievers' mockery of the Prophet as mad and their dismissal of the Qur'an as lunatic rambling; it consoles him, commands patience and forbearance, and warns and gives glad tidings.
TABATABAI:15:9/r1.anchor: بيان تشتمل السورة على الكلام حول استهزاء الكفار بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:15:9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī singles out the promise that God revealed and guards the Reminder as one of the sūra's outstanding verses rich in truths.
TABATABAI:15:9/r5.anchor: ومن غرر الآيات القرآنية المشتملة على حقائق جمة في السورة

TABATABAI:15:9#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r1.claim: The emphatic opening restricts the acts of sending down and preserving to God, answering the rejecters' mockery and demand for angels in the preceding context.
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r1.anchor: صدر الآية مسوق سوق الحصر، وظاهر السياق أن الحصر ناظر إلى ما ذكر

TABATABAI:15:9#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r2.claim: The Qur'an came gradually from God, not from Muhammad or angels; God's complete care preserves this living, enduring remembrance forever.
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r2.anchor: لم تأت به أنت من عندك حتى يعجزوك ويبطلوه بعنادهم وشدة بطشهم

TABATABAI:15:9#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r3.claim: Divine preservation bars additions, omissions, and changes of form or wording that would erase the Qur'an's identity as God's remembrance.
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r3.anchor: مصون من الزيادة عليه بما يبطل به كونه ذكرا، مصون من النقص كذلك، مصون من التغيير

TABATABAI:15:9#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r4.claim: Fussilat likewise calls the Qur'an an invulnerable book that falsehood cannot approach, corroborating its divine protection from distortion.
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r4.anchor: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر لما جاءهم وإنه لكتاب عزيز لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه

TABATABAI:15:9#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r5.claim: The definite article in dhikr is anaphoric, and the active participle lāḥifūn denotes future preservation, as its form ordinarily indicates.
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r5.anchor: أن اللام في الذكر للعهد الذكري وأن المراد بالوصف لحافظون هو الاستقبال

TABATABAI:15:9#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r6.claim: The objection that Torah and Gospel are also called remembrance overlooks context: this promise concerns the Qur'an after its revelation and does not make remembrance itself the cause of preservation.
TABATABAI:15:9#2/r6.anchor: لا دلالة فيها على علية الذكر للحفظ الإلهي ودوران الحكم مداره

TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r7.claim: Historical record establishes that Muhammad claimed prophethood, preached to a community, and brought a book he called the Qur'an and attributed to God; today's Qur'an is generally that same book, not a lost text replaced wholesale.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r7.anchor: من ضروريات التاريخ أن النبي العربي محمدا صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم جاء قبل أربعة عشر قرنا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r8.claim: Some proponents allege only limited additions, omissions, or textual changes, while accepting that most of the revealed book remains as it was in the Prophet's time.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r8.anchor: وإنما احتمل بعض من قال به من المخالف أو المؤالف زيادة شيء يسير كالجملة أو الآية أو النقص أو التغيير

TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r9.claim: The extant Qur'an retains the challenge of unique eloquence throughout its verses, with a striking structure unmatched by preserved or reported Arabic speech.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#6/r9.anchor: فنجده يتحدى بالبلاغة والفصاحة ونجد ما بأيدينا مشتملا على ذلك النظم العجيب البديع لا يعدله ولا يشابهه شيء

TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r1.claim: The Qur'an's challenge that it contains no contradiction is fulfilled by the present text: other verses resolve apparent ambiguities and conflicts.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r1.anchor: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r2.claim: The Qur'an also challenges all humans and jinn to produce its like and calls itself decisive speech without jest; the extant text meets these challenges.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r2.anchor: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن لا يأتون بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r3.claim: The text gives clear truth and guidance to rational principles, natural laws, and moral virtues; its many teachings are unified by tawhid, into which they resolve and from which they derive.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r3.anchor: بل نجد جميع المعارف على سعتها وكثرتها حية بحياة واحدة مدبرة بروح واحد هو مبدء جميع المعارف القرآنية والأصل الذي إليه ينتهي الجميع ويرجع وهو التوحيد

TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r4.claim: Qur'anic accounts of earlier prophets and peoples preserve the purity of religion and prophetic servitude; comparison with corresponding accounts in the two Testaments makes this evident.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r4.anchor: يفصل القول فيها على ما يليق بطهارة الدين ويناسب نزاهة ساحة النبوة وخلوصها للعبودية والطاعة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r5.claim: The Qur'an reports future events explicitly or allusively, and the text in hand confirms those predictions as true.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r5.anchor: يورد آيات في الملاحم ويخبر عن الحوادث الآتية في آيات كثيرة بالتصريح أو بالتلويح

TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r6.claim: The Qur'an describes itself as light and guidance to a straight path and the most upright religion; the extant text loses none of its guidance.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r6.anchor: يصف نفسه بأنه نور وأنه هاد يهدي إلى صراط مستقيم وإلى الملة التي هي أقوم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r7.claim: Dhikr is among the Qur'an's most comprehensive descriptions: it recalls God, His names, attributes and acts, angels, scriptures, messengers, laws, resurrection, and human destinies in Paradise or Hell.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#7/r7.anchor: أنه ذكر لله فإنه يذكر به تعالى بما أنه آية دالة عليه حية خالدة، وبما أنه يصفه بأسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العليا

TABATABAI:15:9#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r1.claim: The present Qur'an loses none of the meanings of remembrance: its many teachings all recall God and constitute the purpose of calling it dhikr.
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r1.anchor: ففي جميع ذلك ذكر الله، وهو الذي يرومه القرآن بإطلاق القول بأنه ذكر ونجد ما بأيدينا من القرآن لا يفقد شيئا

TABATABAI:15:9#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r2.claim: Fussilat says falsehood cannot prevail over or enter the Qur'an at any time through nullification, abrogation, or distortion that would erase its character as remembrance.
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r2.anchor: لا يغلبه باطل ولا يدخل فيه حالا، ولا في مستقبل الزمان لا بإبطال ولا بنسخ ولا بتغيير أو تحريف

TABATABAI:15:9#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r3.claim: The unrestricted wording of remembrance and preservation means God protects the Qur'an against any addition, omission, or change of wording or order that would destroy its remembrance of Him.
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r3.anchor: فقد أطلق الذكر وأطلق الحفظ فالقرآن محفوظ بحفظ الله عن كل زيادة ونقيصة وتغيير في اللفظ أو في الترتيب

TABATABAI:15:9#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r4.claim: The pronoun in lahu cannot refer to the Prophet: the context shows that the polytheists mocked him because of the Qur'an he claimed was revealed to him.
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r4.anchor: ومن سخيف القول إرجاع ضمير " له " إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فإنه مدفوع بالسياق

TABATABAI:15:9#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r5.claim: The revealed Qur'an is divinely guarded from additions, omissions, and changes, as promised to the Prophet; any alteration that erased its described qualities would have left visible effects, which the extant text lacks.
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r5.anchor: فقد تبين مما فصلناه أن القرآن الذي أنزله الله على نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ووصفه بأنه ذكر محفوظ على ما أنزل

TABATABAI:15:9#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r6.claim: The argument rules out distortion that removes Qur'anic qualities, though a fallen repeated verse or a dot or inflection difference could be posited if it affects none of them.
TABATABAI:15:9#3/r6.anchor: فلو فرض سقوط شيء منه أو تغير في إعراب أو حرف أو ترتيب وجب أن يكون في أمر لا يؤثر في شيء من أوصافه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r1.claim: The mutually transmitted hadith al-Thaqalayn says the Prophet left the Qur'an and his family, and that holding to both prevents misguidance; this makes reliance on a corrupted book incoherent.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r1.anchor: حديث الثقلين المتواتر من طرق الفريقين " إني تارك فيكم الثقلين كتاب الله

TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r2.claim: Numerous reports from the Prophet and the Imams command comparing reports with the Qur'an; their unrestricted wording makes them apply beyond legal verses.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r2.anchor: الأخبار الكثيرة الواردة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأئمه أهل البيت عليهم السلام الآمرة بعرض الأخبار على الكتاب

TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r3.claim: The proposal to restrict comparison reports to legal traditions lacks a textual qualifier; fabrication also targets doctrine and prophetic history, as Israelite material illustrates.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r3.anchor: فتخصيصها بذلك تخصيص من غير مخصص. على أن لسان أخبار العرض كالصريح أو هو صريح

TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r4.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r4.claim: The Imams' use of verses matching today's Qur'an, including where isolated distortion reports exist, supports reading many phrases such as kadhā nuzila as explanatory interpretation rather than a variant text, contrasted with inner meaning and ta'wil.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r4.anchor: في الموارد التي فيها آحاد من الروايات بالتحريف، وهذا أحسن شاهد على أن المراد في كثير من روايات التحريف من قولهم عليهم السلام كذا نزل هو التفسير

TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r5.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r5.claim: Reports from Ali and his descendants say the Qur'an held by people is revealed by God despite differing from Ali's codex; their instruction to followers is to read as others do.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r5.anchor: ما بأيدي الناس قرآن نازل من عند الله سبحانه وإن كان غير ما ألفه علي عليه السلام

TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r6.claim: The reports imply differences from Ali's codex concern only surah or verse order where meaning and the Qur'an's divinely described qualities are unaffected; together they establish preservation of those qualities.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r6.anchor: فإنما يخالفه في ترتيب السور أو في ترتيب بعض الآيات التي لا يؤثر اختلال ترتيبها في مدلولها شيئا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r7.claim: Some Shia hadith scholars, Hashwiyya, and some Sunni hadith scholars held that Qur'anic distortion occurred by omission or textual reordering, but not by addition, as no Muslim was said to claim addition.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#8/r7.anchor: ذهب جماعة من محدثي الشيعة والحشوية وجماعة من محدثي أهل السنة إلى وقوع التحريف بمعنى النقص والتغيير في اللفظ أو الترتيب دون الزيادة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r1.claim: Proponents cite numerous Shia and Sunni reports alleging that compilations under Abu Bakr and Uthman omitted or changed passages, words, and letters; some claim two thousand such reports, and al-Alusi calls them beyond count.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r1.anchor: الأخبار الكثيرة المروية من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة الدالة على سقوط بعض السور والآيات وكذا الجمل وأجزاء الجمل والكلمات والحروف

TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r2.claim: They also cite differences among Ibn Masud's codex, Ubayy ibn Kab's, and Uthman's regional copies, varying counts and surah order, along with many anomalous readings transmitted from early Muslims.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r2.anchor: مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود المصحف المعروف مما ينيف على ستين موضعا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r3.claim: A second argument for loss says ordinary reasoning makes a complete, accurate compilation improbable when a non-infallible person gathers a scattered text.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r3.anchor: أن العقل يحكم بأنه إذا كان القرآن متفرقا متشتتا منتشرا عند الناس وتصدى لجمعه غير المعصوم يمتنع عادة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r4.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r4.claim: A third argument says Ali withdrew after the Prophet's death, compiled the Qur'an, presented it as revelation, and was turned away in favor of Zayd's collection; proponents infer that his codex differed, citing his knowledge and a report that truth accompanies him.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#9/r4.anchor: أن عليا عليه السلام اعتزل الناس بعد رحلة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ولم يرتد إلا للصلاة حتى جمع القرآن ثم حمله إلى الناس

TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r1.claim: A fourth argument infers that Muslims must have altered the Qur'an because earlier communities altered their scriptures and reports predict Muslims will imitate them.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r1.anchor: ما ورد من الروايات أنه يقع في هذه الأمة ما وقع في بني إسرائيل حذو النعل بالنعل والقذة بالقذة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r2.claim: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Abu Said reports the Prophet's warning that Muslims will follow earlier peoples step by step, even into a lizard's hole; asked whether he meant Jews and Christians, he replies, who else? The author calls the report widely transmitted from numerous Companions.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r2.anchor: في صحيح البخاري عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال " لتتبعن سنن من كان قبلكم شبرا بشبر

TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r3.speaker: عدة من أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r3.claim: Mustafid Shia routes through several Imams transmit the same prediction and add that Islam's bonds will be undone one by one, beginning with trust and ending with prayer; no separate grading is given.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r3.anchor: من طرق الشيعة عن عدة من أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كما في تفسير القمي

TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r4.claim: Consensus cannot establish absence of additions: it gives probable, not certain, belief, since accumulating agreeing opinions strengthens probability without turning it into certainty.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#10/r4.anchor: الإجماع ليس في نفسه حجة عقلية يقينية بل هو عند القائلين باعتباره حجة شرعية لو أفاد شيئا من الاعتقاد

TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r1.claim: For Sunnis consensus relies on a Prophetic report against communal error; for Shia it depends on an infallible Imam's inclusion or being inferred. Both depend on prophethood, whose living proof is the Qur'an, so possible distortion undermines the proof and consensus. Historical survival of a Qur'an in general does not prove each cited verse untouched.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r1.anchor: حجية الإجماع بالجملة متوقفة على صحة النبوة وذلك ظاهر، وصحة النبوة اليوم متوقفة على سلامة القرآن من التحريف المستوجب لزوال صفات القرآن

TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r2.claim: Treating distortion reports as authoritative traditions is circular for the same reason as consensus; as historical evidence they are isolated, conflicting, not mutawatir or decisive, and few are both sound in chain and conclusive in meaning.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r2.anchor: فلا يبقى للمستدل بها إلا أن يتمسك بها بما أنها أسناد ومصادر تاريخية وليس فيها حديث متواتر ولا محفوف بقرائن قطعية

TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r3.claim: Most such reports have broken or weak chains, and even rare reports sound in chain and meaning are not safe from fabrication or insertion, including Israelite material.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r3.anchor: فإن كثيرا مما وقع فيها من الآيات المحكية من قبيل التفسير وذكر معنى الآيات

TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r4.claim: Some alleged extra Qur'anic passages do not resemble Qur'anic style; even apart from that, reports contradicting the Qur'an are rejected.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#11/r4.anchor: ومع الغض عن ذلك فهي تذكر من الآيات والسور ما لا يشبه النظم القرآني بوجه، ومع الغض عن جميع ذلك فإنها مخالفة للكتاب مردودة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r1.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r1.claim: Al-Kafi reports al-Sadiq explaining that twisting the matter and turning away from what was commanded are deeds God knows; al-Tabataba'i groups this among reports counted as corruption reports.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r1.anchor: في قوله تعالى " وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا " قال " إن تلووا الأمر وتعرضوا عما أمرتم به

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r2.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r2.claim: Some occasion reports recast the verse as commanding the Prophet to convey what was revealed about Ali, and say it was revealed concerning him; they are classified among corruption reports.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r2.anchor: الروايات التي تذكر هذه الآية هكذا " يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل اليك في علي " والآية نازلة في حقه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r3.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r3.claim: Reports say Banu Tamim called the Prophet from outside his chambers, then insert their name into the verse; this led readers to suppose words had dropped from it.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r3.anchor: فذكرت الآية فيها هكذا { إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات } بنو تميم { أكثرهم لا يعقلون } فظن أن في الآية سقطا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r4.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r4.claim: Application reports gloss those who did wrong as Muhammad's family, treating Qur'anic application to later cases as evidence of textual corruption when it is not.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r4.anchor: من الأخبار الواردة في جرى القرآن وانطباقه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r5.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r5.claim: Other application reports interpret obedience to God and the Messenger as allegiance to Ali and the Imams after him, a reading the author says was miscounted among corruption reports.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r5.anchor: وما ورد من قوله { ومن يطع الله ورسوله } في ولاية على والائمة من بعده فقد فاز فوزا عظيما

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r6.speaker: الرضا
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r6.claim: In al-Kafi, al-Rida tells Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi to recite al-Ikhlas as people do, with the added devotional phrase “Thus is my Lord” twice; such additions were mistaken for omitted Qur'an.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r6.anchor: عن عبد العزيز بن المهتدي قال سألت الرضا عليه السلام عن التوحيد فقال كل من قرء قل هو الله أحد وآمن بها فقد عرف التوحيد

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r7.claim: Variants rendering the Badr companions as weak or few instead of humiliated likely paraphrase the meaning, rather than preserve altered Qur'anic wording.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r7.anchor: اختلاف الروايات في لفظ الآية كالتي وردت في قوله تعالى { ولقد نصركم الله ببدر وأنتم أذلة }

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r8.speaker: الإمام
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r8.claim: One report objects that the believers cannot be called humiliated while God's Messenger was among them, supporting a meaning-based explanation of the variants.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r8.anchor: ويؤيده ما ورد في بعضها من قوله عليه السلام لا يجوز وصفهم بأنهم أذلة وفيهم رسول الله

TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r9.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r9.claim: Reports about the stoning verse differ in wording and endings, including whether they mention desire or pleasure and whether the ending says God is Wise or Mighty and Wise; such contradiction can invalidate them.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#12/r9.anchor: وربما لم يكن إلا من التعارض والتنافي بين الروايات القاضي بسقوطها كآية الرجم على ما ورد في روايات الخاصة والعامة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r1.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r1.claim: Transmissions that append material to the Throne Verse give substantially different endings and additions, including divine names and descriptions absent from other versions.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r1.anchor: وكآية الكرسي على التنزيل التي وردت فيها روايات فهي في بعضها هكذا الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects hadith scholars' claim that variant corruption reports remain probative because they agree on the basic claim: their discrepancies weaken the evidence and undermine one another.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r2.anchor: اختلاف هذه الروايات في الآيات المنقولة غير ضائر لاتفاقها في أصل التحريف.

TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r3.claim: Insertion and fabrication are widespread in transmitted reports, as seen in accounts of creation, prophets, earlier peoples, Qur'anic exegesis, and early Islamic events.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r3.anchor: وأما ما ذكرنا من شيوع الدس والوضع في الروايات فلا يرتاب فيه من راجع الروايات المنقولة في الصنع والإيجاد وقصص الأنبياء والأمم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r4.claim: The Qur'an is the secure foundation of religious knowledge and the enduring proof of prophethood, so enemies of religion had strong reason to target it.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r4.anchor: وأعظم ما يهم أمره لأعداء الدين ولا يألون جهدا في إطفاء نوره وإخماد ناره وإعفاء أثره هو القرآن الكريم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r5.claim: If the Qur'an's authority is voided, prophethood and religious teachings lose their proof; the claim that only communal consensus remains cannot rescue them without a further basis for consensus.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r5.anchor: وببطلان حجة القرآن تذهب النبوة سدى والمعارف الدينية لغى لا أثر لها

TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r6.claim: The plausible, evidence-supported possibility that reports were interpolated defeats their legal and rational authority, even when their chains are sound, since sound chains cannot exclude insertion into source books.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#13/r6.anchor: يدفع حجية هذه الروايات ويفسد اعتبارها فلا يبقى معه لها لا حجية شرعية ولا حجية عقلائية

TABATABAI:15:9#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r1.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r1.claim: Several Sunni transmission routes report the prayers called al-Khal' and al-Hafd as suras, but their wording does not resemble Qur'anic composition.
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r1.anchor: كسورتي الخلع والحفد اللتين رويتا بعدة من طرق أهل السنة فسورة الخلع هي بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم اللهم إنا نستعينك ونستغفرك

TABATABAI:15:9#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r2.claim: The alleged surah of al-Wilaya and similar fabrications imitate Qur'anic form but depart from ordinary Arabic and fail to attain the inimitable divine style, which natural taste rejects.
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r2.anchor: ما أورده بعض الروايات من سورة الولاية وغيرها أقاويل مختلقة رام واضعها أن يقلد النظم القرآني فخرج الكلام عن الأسلوب العربي المألوف

TABATABAI:15:9#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r3.claim: Those who accepted fabricated suras were driven by intense deference to reports and neglect of testing them against the Qur'an; a simple look would have shown these were not divine speech.
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r3.anchor: أكثر المعتنين بهذه السور والآيات المختلقة المجعولة إنما دعاهم إلى ذلك التعبد الشديد بالروايات والإهمال في عرضها على الكتاب

TABATABAI:15:9#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r4.claim: The reports conflict with the Qur'an's definitive collective indication, not merely with the apparent wording of the preservation verse or the verse saying falsehood cannot approach it.
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r4.anchor: مجرد مخالفتها لظاهر قوله تعالى { إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون } وقوله { وإنه لكتاب عزيز

TABATABAI:15:9#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r5.claim: The extant Qur'an has a coherent miraculous structure that resolves apparent tensions and fully conveys divine knowledge, with its principles, branches, and parts mutually connected.
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r5.anchor: القرآن الذي بأيدينا متشابه الأجزاء في نظمه البديع المعجز كاف في رفع الاختلافات المتراءاة بين آياته وأبعاضه غير ناقص ولا قاصر في إعطاء معارفه الحقيقية

TABATABAI:15:9#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r6.claim: The opponent's claim that ordinary reality makes alteration impossible is an evident overstatement: reason permits a mismatch between composition and reality unless evidence establishes it, and such evidence was given earlier.
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r6.anchor: أن دعوى الامتناع العادي مجازفة بينة نعم يجوز العقل عدم موافقة التأليف في نفسه للواقع إلا أن تقوم قرائن تدل على ذلك

TABATABAI:15:9#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r7.claim: Ali's gathering and presentation of the Qur'an does not prove disagreement about religious fundamentals or rulings; any difference could concern the ordering of suras or verses revealed over time.
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r7.anchor: جمعه عليه السلام القرآن وحمله إليهم وعرضه عليهم لا يدل على مخالفة ما جمعه لما جمعوه في شيء من الحقائق الدينية الأصلية أو الفرعية

TABATABAI:15:9#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r8.speaker: author
