TABATABAI:15:9#4/r8.claim: Had Ali's collection differed in religious substance, he would have argued the point as he did elsewhere; no transmitted argument has him cite an omitted verse about his authority or accuse them of deletion.
TABATABAI:15:9#4/r8.anchor: ولو كان كذلك لعارضهم بالاحتجاج ودافع فيه ولم يقنع بمجرد إعراضهم عما جمعه واستغنائهم عنه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r1.claim: Preserving Muslim unity cannot explain rejecting Ali's collection only after the community had settled on its own codex; the alleged motive would apply after public distribution, not during collection.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r1.anchor: وهل كان ذلك حفظا لوحدة المسلمين وتحرزا عن شق العصا فإنما كان يتصور ذلك بعد استقرار الأمر واجتماع الناس على ما جمع لهم لا حين الجمع

TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r2.claim: It is implausible that thousands of omitted verses all concerned Ali's authority or were hidden from most Muslims, given the community's desire to learn revelation and the Prophet's effort to teach it.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r2.anchor: هل يسعنا أن ندعي أن ذاك الجم الغفير من الآيات التي يرون سقوطها وربما ادعوا أنها تبلغ الألوف كانت جميعا في الولاية أو كانت خفية مستورة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r3.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r3.claim: Some reports claim over a third of the Qur'an, more than two thousand verses, fell between two passages of al-Nisa; Sunni reports also say al-Tawba once had a basmala and matched al-Baqara, and al-Ahzab was longer than al-Baqara by two hundred lost verses.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r3.anchor: ما يشير إليه بعض المراسيل أنه سقط في آية من أول سورة النساء بين قوله

TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r4.claim: The appeal to abrogation of recitation does not resolve the claims: the interpreters distinguish recitation-and-ruling abrogation from recitation-only abrogation, such as the stoning verse, while other supposedly abrogated rulings remain in the Qur'an.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r4.anchor: كانت منسوخة التلاوة كما ذكره جمع من المفسرين من أهل السنة حفظا لما ورد في بعض رواياتهم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r5.claim: If recitation was abrogated because the passages lacked divine qualities, their removal conflicts with the Qur'an's descriptions of itself as preserved, mighty, free of falsehood, decisive, guidance, light, and a criterion.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r5.anchor: فما معنى الآيات الكثيرة التي تصف القرآن بأنه في لوح محفوظ

TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r6.claim: The broad, unqualified contexts of these descriptions do not permit restricting protection, decisiveness, guidance, light, and miraculousness to only the verses still recited.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r6.anchor: فهل يسعنا أن نقول إن هذه الآيات على كثرتها وإباء سياقها عن التقييد مقيدة بالبعض فبعض الكتاب فقط وهو غير المنسي

TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r7.claim: Making useful speech permanently unrecited and forgotten renders it void and abandoned, which is incompatible with the Qur'an being a reminder.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r7.anchor: وهل جعل الكلام منسوخ التلاوة ونسيا منسيا غير إبطاله وإماتته

TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r8.claim: Al-Tabataba'i concludes that corruption reports transmitted by both Muslim groups, as well as reports that Qur'anic recitation was abrogated, categorically contradict the Qur'an.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#14/r8.anchor: فالحق أن روايات التحريف المروية من طرق الفريقين وكذا الروايات المروية في نسخ تلاوة بعض الآيات القرآنية مخالفة للكتاب مخالفة قطعية

TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r1.claim: Reports comparing this Muslim community's events with those of Israel are well established, but the analogy is not in every respect; reason and necessity rule out that reading.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r1.anchor: لكن هذه الروايات لا تدل على المماثلة من جميع الجهات

TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r2.claim: The analogy concerns shared outcomes and effects; it can refer to sectarian division into 73 Muslim sects, compared with 72 Christian and 71 Jewish sects, a report some call recurrently transmitted.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r2.anchor: فالمراد بالمماثلة هي المماثلة في الجملة من حيث النتائج والآثار

TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r3.claim: The community's division can mean distortion of interpretation: rival groups all rely on the same Book but misplace its words, interpret by opinion, or trust exegesis reports without checking them against scripture.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r3.anchor: من جهة تحريف الكلم عن مواضعه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r4.claim: The analogy reports do not prove textual corruption; the subset that explicitly describes alteration or omission is unsound and contradicts the Qur'an.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r4.anchor: هذه الطائفة على ما بها من السقم مخالفة للكتاب كما تقدم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r5.speaker: اليعقوبي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r5.claim: Yaqubi reports that after heavy Qur'an-reciter deaths at Yamama, Umar pressed Abu Bakr to collect the Qur'an; Abu Bakr initially objected that the Prophet had not done it, then agreed and appointed Quraysh and Ansar to write and consult Sa'id ibn al-As.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r5.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب لأبي بكر يا خليفة رسول الله إن حملة القرآن قد قتل أكثرهم يوم اليمامة فلو جمعت القرآن فإني أخاف عليه أن يذهب حملته

TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r6.speaker: اليعقوبي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r6.claim: A report says Ali collected the Qur'an after the Prophet's death, brought it on a camel, and had divided it into seven parts.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r6.anchor: أن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام كان جمعه لما قبض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأتى به يحمله على جمل فقال هذا القرآن قد جمعته

TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r7.speaker: أبو الفداء
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r7.claim: Abu al-Fida reports that many reciters died fighting Musaylima, so Abu Bakr gathered the Qur'an from oral recitation, palm stalks, and hides, then kept it with Hafsa.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#15/r7.anchor: أمر بجمع القرآن من أفواه الرجال وجريد النخل والجلود

TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r1.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r1.claim: In Bukhari's report, Zayd says Abu Bakr, urged by Umar after Yamama, commissioned him to collect the Qur'an; Zayd gathered it from palm material, stones, and people, found the end of al-Tawba only with Khuzayma, and the sheets passed from Abu Bakr to Umar to Hafsa.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r1.anchor: أخرج البخاري في صحيحه عن زيد بن ثابت قال أرسل إلي أبو بكر مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر بن الخطاب عنده فقال أبو بكر إن عمر أتاني

TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r2.speaker: يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r2.claim: Ibn Abi Dawud transmits that Umar asked people to bring what they had learned from the Prophet, which they had written on sheets, boards, and palm stalks, and required two witnesses before accepting material.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r2.anchor: وكانوا يكتبون ذلك في الصحف والألواح والعسب

TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r3.speaker: عروة
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r3.claim: An interrupted-chain report from Urwa says Abu Bakr told Umar and Zayd to sit at the mosque entrance and write anything brought with two witnesses.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r3.anchor: أن أبا بكر قال لعمر ولزيد اقعدوا على باب المسجد فمن جاءكما بشاهدين

TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r4.speaker: الليث بن سعد
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r4.claim: Ibn Ashta's report says Zayd required two just witnesses for each verse; the final al-Tawba passage was accepted from Abu Khuzayma because the Prophet counted his testimony as two, while Umar's unsupported stoning verse was not written.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r4.anchor: فكان لا يكتب آية إلا بشاهدي عدل

TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r5.speaker: يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Dawud reports that al-Harith ibn Khuzayma brought the final two verses of al-Tawba with testimony that he heard them from the Prophet; Umar confirmed it and said three verses would have formed a separate sura, so these were appended to the last sura.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#16/r5.anchor: فقال عمر وأنا أشهد لقد سمعتهما ثم قال لو كانت ثلاث آيات لجعلتها سورة على حدة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r1.claim: A report from Ubayy says the compilers thought al-Tawba 9:127 was the last revelation, but the Prophet had afterward recited the final two verses of the sura to him.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r1.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أنهم جمعوا القرآن فلما انتهوا إلى الآية التي في سورة براءة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r2.claim: A report attributed to Zayd says the Prophet died before the Qur'an had been gathered into a single object; al-Tabataba'i interprets reports of collecting during the Prophet's life more narrowly below.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r2.anchor: حدثنا إبراهيم بن يسار حدثنا سفيان بن عيينة عن الزهري عن عبيد عن زيد بن ثابت قال قال قبض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يكن القرآن جمع في شيء

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r3.claim: Al-Hakim transmits Zayd saying they arranged the Qur'an from loose sheets in the Prophet's presence.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r3.anchor: وفي مستدرك الحاكم بإسناده عن زيد بن ثابت قال كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نؤلف القرآن من الرقاع

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r4.claim: Al-Tabataba'i takes reports of collection during the Prophet's lifetime to mean joining piecemeal verses to suras or grouping similar suras; a single codex was unquestionably assembled only after his death.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r4.anchor: ولعل المراد ضم بعض الآيات النازلة نجوما إلى بعض السور أو إلحاق بعض السور إلى بعضها مما يتماثل صنفا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r5.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports Ibn Umar saying he had gathered the Qur'an and recited it each night, until the Prophet told him to complete it in a month.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r5.anchor: " عن ابن عمر قال جمعت القرآن فقرأت به كل ليلة فبلغ النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال اقرأه في شهر "

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r6.claim: A report graded hasan says five Ansar gathered the Qur'an during the Prophet's lifetime: Muadh ibn Jabal, Ubada ibn al-Samit, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu al-Darda, and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r6.anchor: بسند حسن عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال جمع القرآن على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم خمسة من الأنصار معاذ بن جبل وعبادة بن الصامت

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r7.speaker: ابن سيرين
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r7.claim: Ibn Sirin's report names Muadh, Ubayy, and Abu Zayd as undisputed collectors during the Prophet's life, while the identity of the fourth is disputed among Abu al-Darda, Uthman, and Tamim al-Dari.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r7.anchor: عن ابن سيرين قال جمع القرآن على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أربعة لا يختلف فيهم معاذ بن جبل وأبي بن كعب وأبو زيد

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r8.speaker: الشعبي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r8.claim: Al-Sha'bi's report lists Ubayy, Zayd, Muadh, Abu al-Darda, Sa'id ibn Ubayd, Abu Zayd, and Mujamma ibn Haritha as collectors in the Prophet's time; one had received all but two or three suras.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r8.anchor: عن الشعبي قال جمع القرآن في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ستة أبي وزيد ومعاذ وأبو الدرداء وسعيد بن عبيد وأبو زيد ومجمع بن حارثة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r9.speaker: ابن بريدة
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Burayda calls Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, the first to gather the Qur'an in a codex; he vowed not to wear his cloak until he had done so.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#17/r9.anchor: عن ابن بريدة قال أول من جمع القرآن في مصحف سالم مولى أبي حذيفة أقسم لا يرتدي برداء حتى يجمعه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r1.claim: The reports just cited show people gathered revealed suras and verses; they do not establish an arrangement matching either today's order or another order. This was the first collection under Abu Bakr.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r1.anchor: أقول أقصى ما تدل عليه هذه الروايات مجرد جمعهم ما نزلت من السور والآيات

TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r2.speaker: اليعقوبي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r2.claim: Yaqubi says Uthman made a second collection amid disagreement and variant readings, grouped long suras together and short ones together, gathered regional codices, then boiled them in water and vinegar or, according to another account, burned them, sparing Ibn Masud's codex.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r2.anchor: وقد جمع القرآن ثانيا في عهد عثمان لما اختلفت المصاحف وكثرت القراءات

TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r3.speaker: اليعقوبي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r3.claim: In Yaqubi's account, Ibn Masud refused to surrender his codex, Uthman had him dragged and broke two ribs, and Aisha protested; Uthman sent standard codices to provinces and required people to read from one copy.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r3.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود بالكوفة فامتنع أن يدفع مصحفه إلى عبد الله بن عامر

TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r4.speaker: اليعقوبي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r4.claim: Yaqubi gives differing explanations for standardization: Uthman heard people claim rival family codices, while another version says Ibn Masud had requested a single copy and Huzayfa had written to him.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r4.anchor: وكان سبب ذلك أنه بلغه أن الناس يقولون قرآن آل فلان

TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r5.speaker: أنس
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r5.claim: Bukhari reports from Anas that Hudhayfa, alarmed by reading disagreements among Syrian and Iraqi troops, urged Uthman to unify the community; Uthman borrowed Hafsa's sheets and appointed Zayd, Ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn al-As, and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith to copy them.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r5.anchor: روى البخاري عن أنس أن حذيفة بن اليمان قدم على عثمان وكان يغازي أهل الشام في فتح أرمينية وأذربيجان مع أهل العراق فأفزع حذيفة اختلافهم في القراءة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r6.speaker: عثمان
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r6.claim: Uthman instructed the three Quraysh scribes to use Quraysh speech if they and Zayd differed, saying the Qur'an had been revealed in their language.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r6.anchor: وقال عثمان للرهط القرشيين الثلاثة إذا اختلفتم أنتم وزيد بن ثابت في شيء من القرآن فاكتبوه بلسان قريش

TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r7.speaker: عثمان
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r7.claim: After copying the sheets, Uthman returned them to Hafsa, sent a copy to every region, and ordered other Qur'anic sheets or codices burned.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r7.anchor: حتى إذا نسخوا الصحف في المصاحف رد عثمان الصحف إلى حفصة وأرسل إلى كل أفق بمصحف مما نسخوا وأمر بما سواه من القرآن

TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r8.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r8.claim: Zayd says that during copying he recalled a verse from al-Ahzab that he had heard the Prophet recite; they found it with Khuzayma ibn Thabit and added it to its sura.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#18/r8.anchor: قال زيد آية من الأحزاب حين نسخنا المصحف قد كنت اسمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ بها فالتمسناها فوجدناها مع خزيمة بن ثابت

TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r1.claim: Abu Qilaba's report says disputes among boys and teachers led Uthman to convene the Companions for a master copy; they consulted someone who had heard the Prophet's reading when verses were disputed and left space for the wording.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r1.anchor: عن أبي قلابة قال حدثني رجل من بني عامر يقال له أنس بن مالك قال اختلفوا في القرآن على عهد عثمان حتى اقتتل الغلمان والمعلمون

TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r2.speaker: كثير بن أفلح
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r2.claim: Ibn Abi Dawud reports that Uthman appointed twelve Quraysh and Ansar to copy sheets from Umar's house; they postponed disputed passages, which Muhammad thought might allow them to consult the latest recitation.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r2.anchor: جمع له اثنى عشر رجلا من قريش والأنصار فبعثوا إلى الربعة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r3.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r3.claim: In a sound-chain report from Suwayd ibn Ghafla, Ali says Uthman acted with the group's agreement; they endorsed unifying readings in one codex to prevent schism and disagreement.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r3.anchor: بسند صحيح عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال علي لا تقولوا في عثمان إلا خيرا فوالله ما فعل الذي فعل في المصاحف إلا عن ملاء منا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r4.speaker: أبي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r4.claim: A report says Uthman proposed dropping the waw in al-Tawba's phrase about those who hoard gold and silver; Ubayy threatened to take up his sword unless it was retained, so they included it.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r4.anchor: عن علباء بن أحمر أن عثمان بن عفان لما أراد أن يكتب المصاحب

TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r5.speaker: عثمان
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r5.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, Uthman explains that the Prophet directed where newly revealed verses belonged; because al-Anfal and al-Tawba had similar stories and he died before clarifying their relation, Uthman placed them together without a basmala.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#19/r5.anchor: قال قلت لعثمان ما حملكم على أن عمدتم إلى الأنفال وهي من المثاني

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r1.speaker: ابن جبير
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r1.claim: The seven long suras are al-Baqara, Al Imran, al-Nisa, al-Maida, al-Anam, al-Araf, and Yunus, according to the cited report and a report from Ibn Jubayr.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r1.anchor: على ما يظهر من هذه الرواية وروي أيضا عن ابن جبير - هي البقرة وآل عمران

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r2.claim: The first collection placed the seven long suras in this order; Uthman later moved al-Anfal and Bara'a between al-Araf and Yunus, with al-Anfal first.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r2.anchor: وقد كانت موضوعة في الجمع الأول على هذا الترتيب ثم غير عثمان هذا الترتيب

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r3.claim: The first collection gathered dispersed written suras and inserted separately revealed verses into suras judged suitable for them.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r3.anchor: الجمع الأول كان جمعا لشتات السور المكتوبة في العسب واللخاف

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r4.claim: The Uthmanic collection consolidated copies after manuscript conflicts and reading differences arose, producing one agreed codex.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r4.anchor: الجمع الثاني وهو الجمع العثماني كان رد المصاحف المنتشرة عن الجمع الأول

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r5.speaker: زيد
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r5.claim: The author notes Zayd's report that he inserted the verse about believers who kept their covenant in al-Ahzab, although copies had circulated fifteen years without it.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r5.anchor: من قول زيد أنه ألحق قوله

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r7.claim: The prominent collection reports, both sound and weak, show an initial gathering of scattered written materials followed by Uthman's consolidation.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r7.anchor: هي أشهر الروايات الواردة في باب جمع القرآن وتأليفه بين صحيحة وسقيمة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r8.claim: These reports are solitary rather than mass-transmitted, but decisive contextual evidence supports confidence in the Quran's preservation.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r8.anchor: أنها آحاد غير متواترة لكنها محفوفة بقرائن قطعية

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r9.claim: The Prophet conveyed everything revealed without concealment and taught and explained revelation to the community, as the Quran states.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r9.anchor: فقد كان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يبلغ الناس ما نزل إليه من ربه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r10.claim: Many Quran learners mastered its recitation and explanation; many readers were killed at the battle of Yamama.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r10.anchor: تعلم تلاوة وبيان وهم القراء الذين قتل جم غفير منهم في غزوة اليمامة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r11.claim: Public eagerness for the Quran and uninterrupted communal engagement meant it never disappeared even briefly before it was gathered in one codex.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r11.anchor: وكان الناس على رغبة شديدة في أخذ القرآن وتعاطيه ولم يترك هذا الشأن

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r12.claim: Continuous public transmission and agreement on a codex kept the Quran from suffering the fate of the Torah, Gospel, and other prophetic books.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r12.anchor: فلم يبتل القرآن بما ابتليت به التوراة والإنجيل وكتب سائر الأنبياء

TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r13.claim: Numerous Sunni and Shiite reports say the Prophet recited many suras in daily prayers and elsewhere before large audiences and identify suras as Meccan or Medinan.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#20/r13.anchor: روايات لا تحصى كثرة وردت من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r2.claim: The strongest evidence is that the Quran now in our hands possesses the noble qualities God attributes to the revealed Quran.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r2.anchor: أعظم الشواهد القاطعة ما تقدم في أول هذه الأبحاث

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r3.claim: The reports establish that the Quran between the covers is God's speech, with no additions or changes; they do not decisively rule out omissions.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r3.anchor: أن الموجود فيما بين الدفتين من القرآن هو كلام الله تعالى

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r4.speaker: عمر
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r4.claim: Reports say Umar repeatedly mentioned a stoning verse that was not written down, leaving omission less than conclusively excluded by the preceding evidence.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r4.anchor: كما روي بعدة طرق أن عمر كان يذكر كثيرا آية الرجم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r5.claim: Al-Tabatabai rejects explaining tahrif reports as abrogation of recitation, judging that doctrine more objectionable than admitting the original claim of alteration.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r5.anchor: على منسوخ التلاوة فقد عرفت فساده وتحققت

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r6.claim: Other companions did not object to the circulating codex, but Ibn Masud omitted al-Falaq and al-Nas, calling them protective prayers revealed for al-Hasan and al-Husayn.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه لم يكتب في مصحفه المعوذتين

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r7.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r7.claim: The other Companions rejected Ibn Masud's claim, and mass-transmitted reports from the Imams of the Prophet's family affirm that both protective suras are Quran.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r7.anchor: وتواترت النصوص من أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام على أنهما

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r8.claim: The reports decisively exclude additions and changes but exclude omissions only probabilistically; claims that they are mass-transmitted in three respects lack evidence.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r8.anchor: نافية للتحريف بالزيادة والتغيير قطعا دون النقص إلا ظنا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r9.claim: The current Quran has the qualities attributed to the actual revelation: decisive speech, resolution of disagreement, reminder, guidance, light, clarification, and a miracle.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r9.anchor: القرآن الذي بأيدينا واجد للصفات الكريمة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r10.claim: The Quran itself proves its divine origin through its qualities; that proof accompanies it wherever it is found, whoever holds it, and however it arrived.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r10.anchor: فحجته معه أينما تحقق وبيد من كان

TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r11.claim: Attribution to the Prophet need not first be established by mass or widespread transmission: the Quran's qualities prove its attribution, unlike ordinary books or sayings.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#21/r11.anchor: فاتصافه بصفاته الكريمة هو الحجة على الاستناد

TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r1.claim: The author concludes that Companions determined sura order in both collections; Uthman's placement of al-Anfal and Bara'a between al-Araf and Yunus is evidence.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r1.anchor: أن ترتيب السور إنما هو من الصحابة في الجمع الأول والثاني

TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r2.claim: Companion codices differed from both official arrangements: Ali's was ordered by revelation, while reports give different orders for Ubay's and Ibn Masud's codices.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r2.anchor: مغايرة ترتيب مصاحف سائر الصحابة للجمع الأول والثاني

TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r3.speaker: الجمهور
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r3.claim: Many scholars hold that sura order was fixed by the Prophet at God's command through Gabriel; some even claim this is established by mass transmission.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r3.anchor: وقد ذهب كثير منهم إلى أن ترتيب السور توقيفي

TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r4.claim: The author asks where the claimed mass transmission is, since the principal reports on collection contain no evidence for divinely fixed sura order.

TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r5.claim: Some support fixed order by reports that the Quran descended all at once from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven; the author postpones discussion of this claim.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r5.anchor: نزول القرآن من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا جملة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r6.claim: The placement of separately revealed verses in their present positions involved Companion judgment, as the first-collection reports indicate.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r6.anchor: مداخلة من الصحابة بالاجتهاد كما هو ظاهر روايات الجمع الأول

TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r8.claim: Even if the Prophet arranged some verses, the reports do not show that the Companions' arrangement matched his in every case; good opinion covers only what they knew.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#22/r8.anchor: ما كانوا ليعمدوا إلى مخالفة ترتيبه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r1.claim: The first-collection reports clearly show that the Companions did not know the position of every verse or even every verse itself.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r1.anchor: أوضح الشواهد على أنهم ما كانوا على علم بمواضع جميع الآيات

TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r2.claim: Reports through Ibn Abbas say the Prophet did not know where one sura ended until the basmala was revealed; al-Bazzar adds that it signaled completion and a new sura.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لا يعرف فصل السورة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r3.claim: Al-Hakim reports from Ibn Abbas that Muslims knew a sura had ended when its basmala was revealed; the author says the chain meets al-Bukhari's and Muslim's standards.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r3.anchor: عن سعيد عن ابن عباس قال كان المسلمون لا يعلمون انقضاء السورة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r4.claim: A further al-Hakim report says that when Gabriel came and recited the basmala, the Prophet knew a sura had begun; the author calls its chain sound.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r4.anchor: عن سعيد عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذا جاءه جبريل

TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r5.speaker: الباقر
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r5.claim: Al-Tabatabai says similar reports occur in other transmissions, including Shiite reports from al-Baqir.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r5.anchor: وروي ذلك من طرق الشيعة عن الباقر

TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r6.claim: These reports imply that verses were ordered for the Prophet by revelation sequence, with Meccan verses in Meccan suras and Medinan verses in Medinan suras, except perhaps one mixed sura.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r6.anchor: الآيات كانت مرتبة عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بحسب ترتيب النزول

TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r7.claim: Therefore, the different present locations of verses result from Companion judgment about placement.

TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r8.claim: Reports on occasions of revelation show many verses in Medinan suras were revealed in Mecca and vice versa, and late revelations occur in suras from early Islam.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#23/r8.anchor: روايات أسباب النزول يدل على كون آيات كثيرة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r2.claim: Verses revealed far apart and placed in suras from a different Meccan or Medinan period are out of revelation order, which the author attributes to Companion judgment.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r2.anchor: في غير موضعها بحسب ترتيب النزول وليس إلا عن اجتهاد من الصحابة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r3.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r3.claim: Ibn Hajar cites a report from Ali that he collected the Quran in revelation order after the Prophet's death; al-Tabatabai says this is a settled implication of Shiite reports.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r3.anchor: ورد عن علي أنه جمع القرآن على ترتيب النزول عقب موت النبي

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r4.speaker: الجمهور
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r4.claim: The majority maintain that verse order was fixed by the Prophet through Gabriel, and that the Companions merely gathered already ordered suras and verses between covers.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r4.anchor: لكن الجمهور أصروا على أن ترتيب الآيات توقيفي

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r5.claim: The author says the details of the first gathering described in the reports plainly refute the majority's interpretation of collection as only physical binding.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r5.anchor: وأنت خبير بأن كيفية الجمع الأول الذي تدل عليها الروايات تدفع هذه الدعوى

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r6.speaker: الزركشي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r6.claim: Al-Zarkashi, as quoted by al-Suyuti, claims consensus that verse order was fixed by revelation.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r6.anchor: نقل السيوطي في الاتقان عن الزركشي دعوى الإجماع عليه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r7.claim: Abu Jafar ibn al-Zubayr is quoted as denying any Muslim disagreement about the fixed ordering.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r7.anchor: عن أبي جعفر بن الزبير نفى الخلاف فيه بين المسلمين

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r8.claim: The author dismisses the reported consensus because it is not authoritative amid disagreement about tahrif and reports that point against fixed order.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r8.anchor: إجماع منقول لا يعتمد عليه بعد وجود الخلاف في أصل التحريف

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r9.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r9.claim: Many scholars also claim that the current order was transmitted from the Prophet by mass transmission; the author calls this surprising and begins to answer with Anas's report.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r9.anchor: تواتر الترتيب الموجود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وهو عجيب

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r10.speaker: أنس
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r10.claim: Anas reports that only four had collected the Quran when the Prophet died: Abu Darda, Muadh, Zayd, and Abu Zayd; another version substitutes Ubay ibn Kab for Abu Darda.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r10.anchor: عن أنس أنه قال مات النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r11.speaker: المازري
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r11.claim: Al-Mazari says there is no argument against transmission in Anas's report: it need not be literal, and collective memorization can preserve the whole even if individuals know only parts.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r11.anchor: عن المازري أنه قال وقد تمسك بقول أنس هذا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r12.claim: One cannot dismiss Anas's apparent wording without a contextual indicator; mere assertion or appeal to others is insufficient in a linguistic argument.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r12.anchor: أما دعواه أن ظاهر كلام أنس غير مراد

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r13.claim: Even a nonliteral reading should mean the four had most of the Quran, not that all Companions had collected the complete Uthmanic text and knew every verse position.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r13.anchor: كان من الواجب أن يحمل على أن هؤلاء الأربعة إنما جمعوا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r14.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TABATABAI:15:1-9#24/r14.claim: Zayd, one of Anas's four and a collector in both official gatherings, states in reports that he had not memorized all verses.

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r1.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r1.claim: A sound-chain report from Muhammad ibn Sirin says Abu Bakr died without collecting the Quran and Umar was killed without collecting it.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن سيرين قال مات أبو بكر ولم يجمع القرآن

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r2.claim: The question of how one knows what really happened applies equally to the claim that the Quran was already completely collected and ordered as asserted.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r2.anchor: فمن أين لهذا القائل أن الواقع في نفس الأمر كما يدعيه

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r3.claim: Distributed memorization can establish transmission of the Quran as a whole, but not mass transmission of each verse in its exact position.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r3.anchor: كون مجموع القرآن من حيث المجموع منقولا بالتواتر

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r4.speaker: البغوي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r4.claim: Al-Baghawi says the Companions bound the Quran between covers without additions or omissions, fearing loss as memorizers died, and wrote it as heard without rearranging it.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r4.anchor: نقل في الإتقان عن البغوي أنه قال في شرح السنة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r5.speaker: البغوي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r5.claim: Al-Baghawi says Gabriel instructed the Prophet about the current order and where each newly revealed verse should be written; the Companions only assembled it in one place.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r5.anchor: نقل في الإتقان عن البغوي أنه قال في شرح السنة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r6.speaker: البغوي
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r6.claim: Al-Baghawi adds that the Quran was written in this order in the Preserved Tablet, descended whole to the lowest heaven, and was then revealed piecemeal; revelation order differs from recitation order.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r6.anchor: نقل في الإتقان عن البغوي أنه قال في شرح السنة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r7.speaker: ابن الحصار
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r7.claim: Ibn al-Hissar says revelation fixed sura order and verse positions, with the Prophet directing where each verse belonged; he claims mass transmission establishes the arrangement.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r7.anchor: ونقل عن ابن الحصار أنه قال ترتيب السور ووضع الآيات مواضعها

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r8.claim: The cited reports establish only which verses were confirmed, not how separately revealed verses were arranged; thus they do not show that Companions copied the Prophet's order without deviation.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r8.anchor: أما قولهم إن الصحابة إنما كتبوا المصحف على الترتيب

TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r10.claim: The Ibn Abbas report conflicts with first-collection accounts and reports that sura endings were recognized by revelation of the basmala.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#25/r10.anchor: الرواية معارضة بروايات الجمع الأول وأخبار نزول بسم الله

TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r2.claim: Reports of the Quran's descent from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven do not say that it was arranged there in the same order as today's codex.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r2.anchor: لكن الروايات ليس فيها أدنى دلالة على كون القرآن

TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r3.claim: The author postpones discussion of the Preserved Tablet and descent to the lowest heaven to his commentary on the opening verses of al-Zukhruf, al-Dukhan, and al-Qadr.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r3.anchor: الكلام في معنى كتابة القرآن في اللوح المحفوظ ونزوله إلى السماء الدنيا

TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r4.claim: The alleged certainty of mass-transmitted current ordering is unsupported, since there is no such transmission for every individual verse.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r4.anchor: هذا التواتر لا خبر عنه بالنسبة إلى كل آية آية

TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r5.claim: Reports say Ibn Masud omitted al-Falaq and al-Nas, treated them as protective prayers rather than Quran, erased them from codices, and never recanted; this challenges universal transmission of their status.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r5.anchor: أن ابن مسعود لم يكتب في مصحفه المعوذتين

TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r6.claim: The author introduces Sunni reports of Quranic forgetting that were used to explain reports of textual omission or alteration.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#26/r6.anchor: وهي عدة روايات وردت من طرق أهل السنة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r2.claim: Because these reports conflict with the Quran's clear wording, the author rejects both the reports of forgetting and those of textual alteration.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r2.anchor: أن هذه الروايات مخالفة لصريح الكتاب فالوجه عطفها على روايات التحريف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the emphatic plural pronouns refer to God Himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد نفسه تبارك وتعالى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r2.claim: Language scholars say a king may use we for himself and his retinue, and this became a customary form even when the ruler acted alone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r2.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: هذا من كلام الملوك؛ الواحد منهم إذا فعل شيئا قال: نحن فعلنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r3.speaker: عامة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r3.claim: The generality of exegetes understand al-dhikr here as the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {نزلنا الذكر} يعني القرآن في قول عامة المفسرين (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r4.claim: Qatada says God protects the revealed Qur'an from Satan adding falsehood or removing truth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: أنزله الله وحفظه من أن يزيد الشيطان فيه باطلا أو يسقط منه حقا (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq likewise says the Qur'an is protected from addition and subtraction, as confirmed by the statement that falsehood cannot approach it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r5.anchor: ونحو هذا قال أبو إسحاق: أن يحفظ من أن يقع فيه زيادة أونقصان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r6.claim: The Companions' collection of the Qur'an in written sheets was one means by which God preserved it; God provided them to do this when He willed its preservation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r6.anchor: جمعهم للقرآن كان من أسباب حفظ الله إياه، ولما أراد حفظه قيضهم لذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the Companions collected the Qur'an to make it easier to access, memorize, and recite; it would not have been lost even without their work because God guaranteed its preservation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r7.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: إنهم أرادوا تسهيل القرآن على الناس وتقريب مطلبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r8.speaker: أصحابنا
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi's associates take the verse as strong proof that the basmala is a Qur'anic verse in every surah: protection from addition and subtraction would otherwise fail, and suspecting the Companions of adding it would also permit suspecting omission.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r8.anchor: قال أصحابنا: هذه الآية دلالة قوية على كون التسمية آية من كل سورة (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r9.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r9.claim: Al-Farra allows the pronoun in lahu to refer to Muhammad, yielding the meaning We are protectors of Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r9.anchor: وحكى الفراء جواز رجوع الكناية في (له) إلى محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- المعنى: وإنا لمحمد حافظون (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbari prefers the pronoun's first referent, the Qur'an: mentioning the sending and the sent thing makes its recipient understood, as in the Qur'an's unexpressed pronoun at 97:1.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r10.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: ولما ذكر الإنزال والمنزل دل ذلك على المنزل عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r11.claim: Al-Wahidi calls the first interpretation clearer and more consistent with the surface sense of the revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p546#3/r11.anchor: والقول الأول هو أوضح القولين، وأحسنها مشابهة لظاهر التنزيل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:5-12/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:5-12/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:5-12/r5.claim: God protects the Qur'an from additions or deletions.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:5-12/r5.anchor: { إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر } القرآن { وإنا له لحافظون } من أن يزاد فيه أو ينقص.

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r3.speaker: cumhur
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r3.claim: The majority says the pronoun in the preservation promise refers to the Reminder, that is, the Qur'an; Elmalılı considers this the more apparent reading.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r3.anchor: buradaki لَهُۥ zamirinde iki vech-i tefsir vardır: Birincisi “zikr”e râci‘olmasıdır

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r4.speaker: Ferrâ ve İbnü’l- Enbârî
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r4.claim: Ferrā and Ibn al-Anbārī take the pronoun to refer to the Messenger, whom God guards from jinn, Satan, and enemies; Elmalılı accepts this as sound but less apparent.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r4.anchor: İkincisi Ferrâ ve İbnü’l- Enbârî kavilleridir ki münzelün aleyh olan Resûlullah’a râci‘olmasıdır

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r5.claim: The Messenger reading is sound, but the wording most readily indicates that the pronoun refers to the Qur'an.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r5.anchor: Bu da sahih bir mâna olmakla beraber âyetten ilk nazarda zâhir olan evvelkisidir

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r6.claim: God undertakes to protect the Qur'an from additions, omissions, distortion, and alteration, guaranteeing its preservation.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r6.anchor: Kur’ân’ın ziyade veya noksan ile tağyir ve tahriften hıfzını taahhüd ve mahfûzan bekāsını ihbar buyurmuştur

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r7.claim: The Companions' collection of the Qur'an into a codex does not conflict with the promise; their effort was one of God's means of preservation and was enabled by Him.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r7.anchor: hâfızların hıfzı gibi onların cem‘i de Allah teâlâ’nın esbâb-ı hıfzı cümlesindendir

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r8.claim: Elmalılı reports exegetes' first account: God's miraculous preservation makes additions or omissions impossible, since altering the Qur'an changes its inimitable composition and the change is recognized.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r8.anchor: Burada müfessirîn Allah teâlâ’nın Kur’ân’ı hıfz etmesinin keyfiyeti hakkında da birkaç vecih beyan etmişlerdir. Şöyle ki: 1. Bunu Allah’ın hıfzı, beşer kelâmına mübâyin bir mucize kılarak

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r9.claim: Elmalılı reports exegetes' second account: God preserves the Qur'an by giving no one the power to produce a counter-imitation, a view close to the first.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r9.anchor: 2. Allah teâlâ hiç kimseye Kur’ân’a mu‘âraza edebilecek kudret vermemek suretiyle onu hıfz u sıyânet etmiştir. Bu iki vecih mütekāribdirler

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r10.claim: Elmalılı reports exegetes' third account: God assigns a community to preserve, teach, and spread the Qur'an among people until the end of the period of religious obligation.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r10.anchor: 3. Allah teâlâ, bekā-yı teklîfin âhirine kadar Kur’ân’ı hıfz u tedris ve halk beyninde neşreder bir cemaati tavzif etmek suretiyle onu halkın ibtâl ü ifsâdından hıfz u sıyânet eder

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r11.claim: Elmalılı reports exegetes' fourth account: any attempted change to a letter, dot, or vowel would be corrected by everyone, even children correcting a great man.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r11.anchor: 4. Hıfzdan murad şudur ki, demişler, bir kimse Kur’ân’ın bir harfini veya bir noktasını değiştirecek olsa bütün âlem ona

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r12.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r12.claim: Razi says no other book has enjoyed the Qur'an's preservation: despite many heretics, Jews, and Christians seeking to corrupt it, it has remained untouched, which is a great miracle.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r12.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Kur’ân’ınki gibi mahfûziyet hiçbir kitaba nasip olmamıştır

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r13.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r13.claim: Razi treats the preservation foretold in this verse, already borne out over nearly six centuries by his time, as a decisive report of the unseen and a compelling miracle.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r13.anchor: Bunca mülhidlerin, Yehûdun, Nasârânın Kur’ân’ı ibtal ve ifsad etmek üzere birçok dâ‘iyeleri bulunduğu hâlde, bu kitabın tahriften her cihetle masûn kalması

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r14.claim: Elmalılı notes that by Hijri 1349, over thirteen and a half centuries after revelation, the promised preservation had become a witnessed intellectual and practical miracle.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r14.anchor: hicret-i seniyyenin bin üç yüz kırk dokuzuncu senesinde

ELMALILI:15:8-9/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r15.claim: Even without this explicit prediction, the Qur'an's uniquely long preservation would itself be a practical miracle; the verse's emphatic foretelling makes it an intellectual miracle too.
ELMALILI:15:8-9/r15.anchor: on üç buçuk asırdan ziyade bir müddetten beri cihan böyle hem ilmî ve hem amelî haysiyeti câmi‘bir mucizenin şâhidi olagelmiştir

ELMALILI:v1p105/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p105/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p105/r1.claim: In the sense illustrated by 21:24, Qur’an is named al-Dhikr; 15:9 and 3:58 are cited as Qur’anic uses of that name.
ELMALILI:v1p105/r1.anchor: İşte bu mâna ile Kur’ân’ın bir ismi de “ez-Zikr”dir: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ

ELMALILI:v1p105/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p105/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p105/r2.claim: The Qur’an is also called al-Ḥukm; Elmalılı says the meaning of that name was discussed earlier.

ELMALILI:v1p105/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p105/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p105/r3.claim: The Qur’an is also called rūḥ, since it is the spirit of a great spiritual life; 42:52 is cited for this name, and these names are all found in the Qur’an.
ELMALILI:v1p105/r3.anchor: Kur’ân’a “rûh” da denilmiştir. Çünkü büyük bir hayât-ı ma‘- neviyenin rûhudur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r1.claim: Dhikr refers to the Qur'an and Book named in the surah's opening verse, both terms used especially for the revelation addressed to Muhammad; the commentary translates it as revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r1.anchor: Zikir kelimesi, sûrenin ilk âyetinde geçen ve ikisi de özellikle Hz. Peygamber’in muhatap olduğu ilâhî vahiy için kullanılan Kur’an ve kitabı ifade etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r2.claim: Verse 9 directly rejects the mockery in verse 6 that Muhammad received no revelation and was mad, with words from jinn or meaningless ravings rather than God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r2.anchor: Yukarıda 6. âyette müşrikler alaylı bir ifadeyle, Hz. Muhammed’e vahiy diye bir şey gelmediğini ima etmişler ve onun bir mecnun olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r3.claim: In context, dhikr is revelation and preservation means shielding it during revelation from outside influence that could compromise its divine character; the verse rejects claims of nondivine origin or additions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r3.anchor: Şu halde burada “zikir”den maksat vahiy, korumadan maksat da vahiy sürecinde âyetlerin ilâhî olma özelliğini bozacak şekildeki herhangi bir dış etkiden vahyin korunmasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r4.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r4.claim: Tabari interprets the promise as preventing false words or errors from entering the Qur'an and preventing omissions from its rulings, limits, and obligations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r4.anchor: Taberî, âyeti “Biz muhakkak ki Kur’an’ı koruyup içine onun aslında bulunmayan bir ifadenin, bir yanlışın karışmasını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r5.claim: Most commentators and scholars adopt preservation against later intervention: unlike earlier scriptures, the Qur'an will not be diminished, altered, corrupted, or lost, but remain intact until the Resurrection by God's certain promise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r5.anchor: bu yorum, müfessirlerin ve diğer âlimlerin büyük çoğunluğunca da benimsenmiştir. Buna göre daha önceki kutsal kitapların mâruz kaldığı ve genellikle tahrif terimiyle ifade edilen eksilme, değişme, bozulma, kaybolma gibi haller Kur’an’ın başına gelmeyecek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r6.claim: Muslims treated preservation as a sacred duty and transmitted the Qur'an in its original form, first through memorization and later through both memorization and writing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r6.anchor: Peygamber’in ağzından söz olarak dışa yansıdığı günden bugüne kadar bütün müslümanlar Kur’an’ı korumayı en kutsal görev bilmişler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r7.claim: The development of writing tools, especially digital media, makes preserving the Qur'anic text easier today and in the future.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r7.anchor: Çeşitli yazım imkânlarının, özellikle dijital ortamın geliştiği günümüzde ve bundan sonraki dönemlerde ise kuşkusuz Kur’an metninin korunması daha kolay olacaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r8.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r8.claim: Some infer that the basmala at the start of each surah is part of that surah and its first verse, since a later addition would conflict with this preservation promise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r8.anchor: böyle bir ekleme de konumuz olan âyetin hükmüne aykırıdır (Râzî, XIX, 166)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r9.claim: The author rejects that basmala inference as an unsound interpretation arising from excessive concern about Qur'anic preservation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r9.anchor: Ancak bunun Kur’an’ın korunmuşluğu üzerine aşırı hassasiyetten kaynaklanan isabetsiz bir yorum olduğu kanaatindeyiz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r10.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r10.claim: Some interpreters take the one promised protection for to be the Prophet himself; God shielded him through severe opposition and enabled an unprecedented success in spreading Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r10.anchor: Âyetin “...ve onu mutlaka koruyacak olan da yine biziz” kısmında, korunacağı bildirilenin Hz. Peygamber olduğuna dair görüşler de vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r11.claim: Since protecting the Prophet also indirectly protects revelation, the author says the Prophet-protection and revelation-protection interpretations can be combined.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:9/r11.anchor: Kuşkusuz Peygamber’in korunması, dolaylı olarak vahyin de korunması anlamını içerdiğinden her iki yorumu birleştirmek mümkündür

BURHAN:v2p43/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p43/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p43/r6.claim: The Qurʾan is internally consistent and mutually supportive, and God has undertaken to preserve it.
BURHAN:v2p43/r6.anchor: وأنه الكتاب المهيمن على غيره وهو في نفسه متعاضد وقد تولى الله حفظه

BURHAN:v2p71/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p71/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p71/r1.claim: Ambiguous passages about God's essence, attributes, actions, and metaphorical wording are resolved by clear principles affirming God's incomparability and oneness.
BURHAN:v2p71/r1.anchor: الأول الأشياء التي يجب ردها عند الإشكال إلى أصولها

BURHAN:v2p71/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p71/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p71/r2.claim: For prophecy and the description of revelation, the decisive principles are that God preserves the Reminder and that the Prophet does not speak from desire.
BURHAN:v2p71/r2.anchor: ومنه ضرب في تفصيل ذكر النبوة ووصف إلقاء الوحي

BURHAN:v2p71/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p71/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p71/r4.claim: Some passages admit many plausible interpretations, and the intended specific meaning cannot be decisively known to us.
BURHAN:v2p71/r4.anchor: ومنه الآيات التي اختلف المفسرون فيها على أقوال كثيرة تحتملها الآية ولا يقطع على واحد من الأقوال

BURHAN:v2p124/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p124/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p124/r1.claim: Relative eloquence and verbal grace cannot be proved by formal logic; they are recognized through taste, like subtle differences in beauty.
BURHAN:v2p124/r1.anchor: اعلم أن معرفة الفصيح والأفصح والرشيق والرشق والجلى والأجلى والعلى والأعلى من الكلام أمر لا يدرك إلا بالذوق

BURHAN:v2p124/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p124/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p124/r2.claim: Not every grammarian, linguist, or jurist has literary taste; trained readers of rhetoric who practice prose, speeches, writing, and poetry judge the relative quality of speech.
BURHAN:v2p124/r2.anchor: وليس كل من اشتغل بالنحو أو باللغة أو بالفقه

BURHAN:v2p124/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p124/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p124/r3.claim: Scholars agree that the Quran's wording and components must be mass-transmitted; the verified Sunni position also requires mass transmission of placement and order.
BURHAN:v2p124/r3.anchor: النوع التاسع والثلاثون معرفة وجوب تواتره لاخلاف أن كل ما هو من القرآن يجب أن يكون متواترا فى أصله وأجزائه

BURHAN:v2p124/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p124/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p124/r4.claim: The author argues that preservation and universal proclamation require mass transmission throughout the Quran's wording, location, and order; singularly transmitted material is not Quran.

BURHAN:v2p124/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p124/r5.speaker: كثير من الأصوليين
BURHAN:v2p124/r5.claim: Many legal theorists require tawatur for Quranic wording alone, not placement or order; they point to al-Shafi'i's proof for the basmala at each surah's beginning.
BURHAN:v2p124/r5.anchor: وذهب كثير من الأصوليين إلى أن التواتر شرط في ثبوت ما هو من القرآن بحسب أصله وليس بشرط فى محله ووضعه

TABATABAI:2:21-25#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#6/r5.claim: The Qur'an also challenges through predictions: Rome's reversal, Muhammad's return to Mecca, safe entry into the sanctuary, events involving booty, divine protection of the Prophet, and preservation of revelation.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#6/r5.anchor: ومنها الإخبار عن الحوادث المستقبلة كقوله تعالى غلبت الروم في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون في بضع سنين

ITQAN:v1p160/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160/r1.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ITQAN:v1p160/r1.claim: A report attributed to Zayd ibn Thabit says the Prophet died while the Qurʾan had not been collected into one thing.
ITQAN:v1p160/r1.anchor: قال الديرعاقولي في فوائده حدثنا إبراهيم بن بشار حدثنا سفيان بن عيينة عن الزهري عن عبيد عن زيد بن ثابت قال قبض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يكن القرآن جمع في شيء

ITQAN:v1p160/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160/r2.speaker: الخطابي
ITQAN:v1p160/r2.claim: Al-Khattabi explains that the Qurʾan was not assembled as a codex during the Prophet's life because further abrogation of rulings or recitation was expected; after revelation ended, the caliphs began collection with Abu Bakr on Umar's advice.
ITQAN:v1p160/r2.anchor: قال الخطابي إنما لم يجمع صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن في المصحف لما كان يترقبه من ورود ناسخ لبعض أحكامه أو تلاوته فلما انقضى نزوله بوفاته ألهم الله الخلفاء الراشدين ذلك

ITQAN:v1p160/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p160/r3.speaker: الخطابي
ITQAN:v1p160/r3.claim: Al-Khattabi says the ḥadith forbidding writing anything from the Prophet besides the Qurʾan does not conflict: Qurʾan had all been written, but not collected in one place or arranged by sura.
ITQAN:v1p160/r3.anchor: وقد كان القرآن كتب كله في عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لكن غير مجموع في موضع واحد ولا مرتب السور

ITQAN:v3p94#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r9.speaker: بعض الأقدمين
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r9.claim: The Qur’an uses plural forms such as We sent down and We apportioned for God alone as a form of grandeur and exaltation.
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r9.anchor: والأبهة مثل ﴿ إنا أرسلنا ﴾ ﴿ نحن قسمنا ﴾ عبر بالصيغة الموضوعة للجماعة للواحد تعالى تفخيما وتعظيما وأبهة

DAMGHANI:v1p182/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r1.claim: Dhikr can mean the Qur'an; Dāmghānī groups this with references calling it blessed remembrance and asking whether people would be left without it.
DAMGHANI:v1p182/r1.anchor: " إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر " وقوله تعالى في سورة الأنبياء " وهذا ذكر مبارك أنزلناه "

DAMGHANI:v1p137/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r8.claim: Ḥifẓ also means keeping or guarding itself, illustrated by 13:11, 15:9, and protection from rebellious Satan in 37:7.
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r8.anchor: الثالث : الحفظ بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة الرعد " يحفظونه من أمر الله " كقوله تعالى في سورة الحجر

JISHUMI:v1p195/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p195/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p195/r3.claim: Dhikr may mean God’s reminder of obligations and rulings to His servants, or an honor for those who adhere to it.
JISHUMI:v1p195/r3.anchor: قيل: إنه ذكر من الله تعالى لعباده بالفرائض والأحكام،
